'Master,' he said, 'you turned five 75-pound bags <I>of silver</I> over to me. Look, I gained another five 75-pound bags <I>of silver</I>.'</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 25:21"></A><SPAN class="verseno">21 </SPAN>'Well done,' his master declared. 'You are a good and reliable slave. Since you were reliable with these few things of mine, I will put you in charge of many things. Come, be happy with your master.'</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 25:22"></A><SPAN class="verseno">22 </SPAN>The slave who received two 75-pound bags <I>of silver (worth $600,000)</I> also came forward. 'Master,' he said, 'you turned two 75-pound bags <I>of silver</I> over to me. Look, I gained another two 75-pound bags <I>of silver</I>.'</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 25:23"></A><SPAN class="verseno">23 </SPAN>'Well done,' his master declared. 'You are a good and reliable slave. Since you were reliable with these few things of mine, I will put you in charge of many things. Come, be happy with your master.'</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 25:24"></A><SPAN class="verseno">24 </SPAN>The slave who had received one 75-pound bag <I>of silver (worth $300,000)</I> also came forward. 'Master,' he said, 'I knew that you are a harsh man. You harvest where you didn't plant, and you gather things up from the places where you didn't disperse anything.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 25:25"></A><SPAN class="verseno">25 </SPAN>And because I was afraid, I went off and hid your 75-pound bag <I>of silver</I> in the ground. Look, here's your money.'</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 25:26"></A><SPAN class="verseno">26 </SPAN>His master responded by saying, 'Evil and lazy slave, you realized that I harvest where I didn't plant and I gather things up from the places where I didn't disperse anything.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 25:27"></A><SPAN class="verseno">27 </SPAN>So you should have at least thrown my silver coins to the banker. That way when I came I could retrieve my money with interest.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 25:28"></A><SPAN class="verseno">28 </SPAN>Take the 75-pound bag <I>of silver</I> away from him, and give it to the slave with ten 75-pound bags <I>of silver (worth $3 million)</I>.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 25:29"></A><SPAN class="verseno">29 </SPAN>You see, everyone who has something will be given more, and it will overflow, but the person who has nothing, even what he has will be taken away from him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 25:30"></A><SPAN class="verseno">30 </SPAN>And throw the unneeded slave out into the darkness that is outside and further away. There he will cry and grind his teeth.'</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 25:31"></A><SPAN class="verseno">31 </SPAN>When the Son of the Person comes in His magnificence with all the angels, at that time, He will be seated on a throne of His magnificence.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 25:32"></A><SPAN class="verseno">32 </SPAN>And all the nations will be gathered together in front of Him. He will isolate them away from each other, like a shepherd isolates the sheep away from the goats.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 25:33"></A><SPAN class="verseno">33 </SPAN>He will certainly position the sheep to the right of Him, but the little goats to the left.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 25:34"></A><SPAN class="verseno">34 </SPAN>Then the King will state to the sheep to the right of Him, 'Come on, My Father has conferred blessings on you, inherit the monarchy that has been readied for you since the world was formed.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 25:35"></A><SPAN class="verseno">35 </SPAN>You see, I was hungry, and you gave Me something to eat. I was thirsty, and you gave Me a drink. I was a stranger, and you took Me home with you.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 25:36"></A><SPAN class="verseno">36 </SPAN>I was naked, and you threw a robe around Me. I was in frail health, and you kept an eye on Me. I was in jail, and you came to Me.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 25:37"></A><SPAN class="verseno">37 </SPAN>Then the people who did what is right will respond to Him, 'Master, when did we see You hungry and feed You, or thirsty and give You a drink?</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 25:38"></A><SPAN class="verseno">38 </SPAN>When did we see You a stranger and take You home with us, or naked and throw a robe around You?</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 25:39"></A><SPAN class="verseno">39 </SPAN>When did we see You in frail health or in jail and come to You?'</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 25:40"></A><SPAN class="verseno">40 </SPAN>The King will answer them by stating, 'Amen, I tell you, as much as you did to one of these smallest brothers of Mine, you did to Me.'</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 25:41"></A><SPAN class="verseno">41 </SPAN>Then He will also state to the <I>goats</I> to the left of Him, 'Travel away from Me, you who have been cursed, to the fire that spans all time, the fire that has been readied for the Accuser and his angels.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 25:42"></A><SPAN class="verseno">42 </SPAN>You see, I was hungry, and you didn't give Me anything to eat. I was thirsty, and you didn't give Me a drink.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 25:43"></A><SPAN class="verseno">43 </SPAN>I was a stranger, and you didn't take Me home with you; naked, and you didn't throw a robe around Me; in frail health and in jail, and you didn't keep an eye on Me.'</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 25:44"></A><SPAN class="verseno">44 </SPAN>Then they will also respond by saying, 'Master, when did we see You hungry, or thirsty, or a stranger, or naked, or in frail health, or in jail, and didn't serve You?'</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 25:45"></A><SPAN class="verseno">45 </SPAN>Then He'll answer them, 'Amen, I tell you, as much as you didn't do for one of these smallest ones, you didn't do for Me either.'</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 25:46"></A><SPAN class="verseno">46 </SPAN>These will go off into confinement that spans all time. But those who did what is right will go into life that spans all time."</P>
<TITLE>Matthew 26</TITLE>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:1"></A><SPAN class="verseno">1 </SPAN>When Jesus happened to finish all these messages, He told His students,</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:2"></A><SPAN class="verseno">2 </SPAN>"You realize that after two days the Passover will happen and the Son of the Person will be turned in to be nailed to a cross."</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:3"></A><SPAN class="verseno">3 </SPAN>At the time <I>that He was saying this</I>, the head priests and the ethnic group's older men were gathered together in the head priest Caiaphas's courtyard.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:4"></A><SPAN class="verseno">4 </SPAN>Together they advised to deceptively arrest Jesus and kill Him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:5"></A><SPAN class="verseno">5 </SPAN>But they were saying, "Not at the festival so that a riot doesn't happen among the group."</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:6"></A><SPAN class="verseno">6 </SPAN><I>Later</I>, Jesus happened to be in Bethany in Simon's house, the one that had a skin disease.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:7"></A><SPAN class="verseno">7 </SPAN>A woman came with an alabaster jar of high-priced perfume. She spilled it down on Jesus' head as He was feasting and chatting.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:8"></A><SPAN class="verseno">8 </SPAN>When the students saw it, they were frustrated. "Why did she ruin this high-priced perfume?" they said.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:9"></A><SPAN class="verseno">9 </SPAN>"You see, it could have been put up for sale for a lot of money. That money could have been given to the poor."</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:10"></A><SPAN class="verseno">10 </SPAN>When Jesus knew it, He said, "Why are you bothering the woman? You see, she has worked to do nice work for Me.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:11"></A><SPAN class="verseno">11 </SPAN>You will always have poor people with you, but you won't always have Me.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:12"></A><SPAN class="verseno">12 </SPAN>You see, when she put this perfume on My body, she did it with a specific goal--to prepare Me for burial.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:13"></A><SPAN class="verseno">13 </SPAN>Amen, I tell you, wherever this good news is spoken publicly in the whole world, what she did will also be spoken for a reminder of her."</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:14"></A><SPAN class="verseno">14 </SPAN>At that time, one of the Twelve, the one called Judas from Kerioth, traveled to the head priests.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:15"></A><SPAN class="verseno">15 </SPAN>"How much do you want to give me," he said, "if I turn Him over to you?" The head priests stacked up thirty silver coins for him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:16"></A><SPAN class="verseno">16 </SPAN>From then on, he looked for a good time to turn Him over to them.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:17"></A><SPAN class="verseno">17 </SPAN>The students went to Jesus concerning the first day of the Yeast-free Festival and said, "Where do You want us to get things ready for You to eat the Passover meal?"</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:18"></A><SPAN class="verseno">18 </SPAN>"Make your way back into the city to [NAME REDACTED]," He said, "and tell him, 'The Teacher says, My time is near. I am doing the Passover at your place with My students.'"</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:19"></A><SPAN class="verseno">19 </SPAN>The students did as Jesus dictated and they got the Passover meal ready.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:20"></A><SPAN class="verseno">20 </SPAN>When evening came, He was feasting and chatting with the Twelve.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:21"></A><SPAN class="verseno">21 </SPAN>As they ate, He said, "Amen, I tell you that one person from you will turn Me in."</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:22"></A><SPAN class="verseno">22 </SPAN>They were terribly sad. They began to say to Him, each one, "It isn't me, is it, Master?"</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:23"></A><SPAN class="verseno">23 </SPAN>When Jesus answered, He said, "The one who dipped <I>his bread</I> in the bowl with my hand will turn Me in.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:24"></A><SPAN class="verseno">24 </SPAN>The Son of the Person certainly will make His way back just as the Bible says, but what a tragedy it is to the person that turns Him in. It would have been better for him not to be born.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:25"></A><SPAN class="verseno">25 </SPAN>Judas (the one who would turn Him in) responded by saying, "It isn't me, is it, Rabbi?" "You said it," said Jesus.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:26"></A><SPAN class="verseno">26 </SPAN>As they were eating, Jesus took bread, conferred a blessing on it, and split it. He gave it to the students and said, "Take it. Eat it. This is My body."</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:27"></A><SPAN class="verseno">27 </SPAN>He took a cup, was thankful, and gave it to them. "Everyone, drink from it," He said.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:28"></A><SPAN class="verseno">28 </SPAN>"You see, this is My blood that seals the deal. It is spilled out concerning many people for a forgiveness of sins.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:29"></A><SPAN class="verseno">29 </SPAN>I tell you, I won't in anyway drink juice from a grapevine from now on until that day when I drink it new with you in My Father's monarchy."</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:30"></A><SPAN class="verseno">30 </SPAN>After they sang praise songs, they went out to the Mount of Olives.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:31"></A><SPAN class="verseno">31 </SPAN>At that time, Jesus said to them, "Tonight, all of you will stumble on Me. You see, the Bible says, 'I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep in His flock will disperse' <I>(Zechariah 13:7)</I>.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:32"></A><SPAN class="verseno">32 </SPAN>After I am gotten up, I will lead the way ahead of you into Galilee."</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:33"></A><SPAN class="verseno">33 </SPAN>Peter responded by saying, "Even if all of them stumble on You, I will never ever stumble."</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:34"></A><SPAN class="verseno">34 </SPAN>"Amen, I tell you," Jesus declared, "tonight before it is time for the rooster to crow, you will flatly deny Me three times."</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:35"></A><SPAN class="verseno">35 </SPAN>"Even if I have to die with You," Peter said, "I will not in any way flatly deny You." All the students also said similar things.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:36"></A><SPAN class="verseno">36 </SPAN>At that time, Jesus went with them onto a parcel of land called Gethsemane. "Be seated here," He said to His students, "while I go off to there and pray."</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:37"></A><SPAN class="verseno">37 </SPAN>He took Peter and the two sons of Zebedee along with Him. He began to be sad and heavyhearted.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:38"></A><SPAN class="verseno">38 </SPAN>At that time He told them, "My soul is overcome with sadness up to death. Stay here. Stay awake with Me."</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:39"></A><SPAN class="verseno">39 </SPAN>He went on ahead a little, got down on His face, and prayed. "My Father," He said, "if it is possible, this cup must pass away from Me. But more importantly, it should not be as I want it. It should be as You want it."</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:40"></A><SPAN class="verseno">40 </SPAN>He came to His students and found them sleeping. "Is this how it is?" He said to Peter. "Didn't you have enough strength to stay awake with Me for one hour?</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:41"></A><SPAN class="verseno">41 </SPAN>Stay awake. Pray so that you won't get into trouble. The spirit certainly is eager, but the physical body is weak."</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:42"></A><SPAN class="verseno">42 </SPAN>Again He went off a second time and prayed. "My Father," He said, "if this can't pass unless I drink it, what You want must happen."</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:43"></A><SPAN class="verseno">43 </SPAN>When He came to His students again, He found them sleeping. You see, their eyes had been weighted down.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:44"></A><SPAN class="verseno">44 </SPAN>He left them again, went off, and prayed a third time. He again said the same words.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:45"></A><SPAN class="verseno">45 </SPAN>At that time, He came to the students and said, "Sleep for the rest of the time and relax." <I>After some time,</I> Jesus said, "Look, the time has come near. The Son of the Person will soon be turned over to sinful people's hands.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:46"></A><SPAN class="verseno">46 </SPAN>Get up. Let's lead the way. Look, the person turning Me in has come near."</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:47"></A><SPAN class="verseno">47 </SPAN>As He was still speaking, look, Judas, one of the Twelve, came with a big crowd. The crowd had daggers and wooden clubs. They were sent to Him by the head priests and the ethnic group's older men.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:48"></A><SPAN class="verseno">48 </SPAN>Judas gave them <I>a way for him to</I> indicate <I>who it is</I>: "Whoever I am friendly with is Him. Take Him into custody."</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:49"></A><SPAN class="verseno">49 </SPAN>Right away he came up to Jesus and was being very friendly to Him. "Happy to see You, Rabbi," he said.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:50"></A><SPAN class="verseno">50 </SPAN>"Comrade," Jesus said, "on to what you are here for." At that time, they came up, put their hands on Jesus, and took Him into custody.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:51"></A><SPAN class="verseno">51 </SPAN>And look, one of the ones with Jesus put out his hand, pulled out his dagger, struck the head priest's slave, and cut off his earlobe.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:52"></A><SPAN class="verseno">52 </SPAN>"Return your dagger back into its place," Jesus said. "You see, all who take a dagger will be ruined by a dagger.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:53"></A><SPAN class="verseno">53 </SPAN>Or do you think that I can't call My Father here and He will now stand up more than twelve legions <I>(Latin for regiments)</I> of angels here <I>to protect Me?</I></P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:54"></A><SPAN class="verseno">54 </SPAN><I>But if I did that,</I> how, then, would the <I>Old Testament</I> writings be accomplished, the ones that say it must happen like this?"</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:55"></A><SPAN class="verseno">55 </SPAN>In that hour, Jesus said to the crowds, "Did you come out to apprehend Me with daggers and wooden clubs as if I were a bandit? Everyday I was seated on the temple grounds teaching. <I>How is it that</I> you didn't take Me into custody then?</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:56"></A><SPAN class="verseno">56 </SPAN>But this whole thing has happened so that what the preachers' writings say, might be accomplished." At that time, all the students left Him and escaped.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:57"></A><SPAN class="verseno">57 </SPAN>The <I>underlings</I> took Jesus into custody and led Him off to the head priest Caiaphas where the Old Testament transcribers and older men were gathered together.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:58"></A><SPAN class="verseno">58 </SPAN>Peter was following Him at a distance until they came to the head priest's courtyard. He went inside the courtyard and sat with the underlings to see the conclusion.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:59"></A><SPAN class="verseno">59 </SPAN>The head priests and the whole council were looking for a witness who would tell a lie about Jesus that they could use to put Him to death.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:60"></A><SPAN class="verseno">60 </SPAN>But they didn't find any among the many lying witnesses that came forward. Later, two witnesses came forward.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:61"></A><SPAN class="verseno">61 </SPAN>They said, "This Person was declaring, 'I can tear God's temple down and build it back up in three days.'"</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:62"></A><SPAN class="verseno">62 </SPAN>The head priest stood up and said to Him, "Aren't You going to answer anything? What are these witnesses saying against you?"</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:63"></A><SPAN class="verseno">63 </SPAN>But Jesus kept silent. "I am forcing you into an oath under the living God," the head priest said, "to tell us if you are the Anointed King, God's Son."</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:64"></A><SPAN class="verseno">64 </SPAN>"You said it," Jesus said. "More importantly, I tell you, after this you will see the Son of the Person sitting at the right side of the Ability and coming on the clouds of the sky."</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:65"></A><SPAN class="verseno">65 </SPAN>At that time, the head priest ripped his clothes apart <I>(to show how appalled he was by this)</I> and said, "He insulted God. What? Do we still need witnesses? Look. Now you heard His insult.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:66"></A><SPAN class="verseno">66 </SPAN>What do you think?" When they answered, they said, "He is eligible to be sentenced to death."</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:67"></A><SPAN class="verseno">67 </SPAN>Then they spit in His face and slugged Him. The people slapped Him,</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:68"></A><SPAN class="verseno">68 </SPAN>saying, "Preach to us, Anointed King. Tell us who struck You."</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:69"></A><SPAN class="verseno">69 </SPAN>But Peter was sitting out in the courtyard. One servant girl came up to him and said, "You also were with Jesus, the Galilean."</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:70"></A><SPAN class="verseno">70 </SPAN>He denied it in front of everyone. "I don't know what you are saying," he said.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:71"></A><SPAN class="verseno">71 </SPAN>When he went out into the gateway, another girl saw him. "This person was there with Jesus, the Nazarene," she said to the people.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:72"></A><SPAN class="verseno">72 </SPAN>Again he denied it, this time with an oath. "I don't know the person," he said.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:73"></A><SPAN class="verseno">73 </SPAN>After a little while, the people standing there came up to Peter and said, "You truly are one of them. You see, your speech makes it obvious."</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:74"></A><SPAN class="verseno">74 </SPAN>At that time, he began to vow under the penalty of being doomed and to guarantee, "I don't know the person." Right away a rooster crowed.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 26:75"></A><SPAN class="verseno">75 </SPAN>Peter remembered the statement that Jesus had stated: "Before it is time for the rooster to crow, you will flatly deny Me three times." He went outside and cried bitterly.</P>
<TITLE>Matthew 27</TITLE>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:1"></A><SPAN class="verseno">1 </SPAN>When it became morning, all the head priests and the ethnic group's older men received counsel on how they would put Jesus to death.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:2"></A><SPAN class="verseno">2 </SPAN>After they tied Him up, they led Him off to <I>the Roman leader of that area,</I> Pilate, and turned Him over to him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:3"></A><SPAN class="verseno">3 </SPAN>At that time, when Judas (the one who turned Him in) saw that He was found guilty, he regretted what he had done and returned the thirty silver coins to the head priests and older men.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:4"></A><SPAN class="verseno">4 </SPAN>"I sinned when I turned in blood that is not guilty," he said. But the head priests said, "What is that to us? <I>It's your problem.</I> You will see <I>to it</I>."</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:5"></A><SPAN class="verseno">5 </SPAN>He tossed the silver coins into the temple, took a back way, went off, and hung himself.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:6"></A><SPAN class="verseno">6 </SPAN>When the silver coins were given to the head priests, they said, "We aren't allowed to put this into the Corban <I>(the name of the offering boxes at the temple)</I> since it is a price of blood <I>(a payment for someone's life)</I>."</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:7"></A><SPAN class="verseno">7 </SPAN>After receiving counsel, they purchased the clay worker's field with it for the burial of strangers.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:8"></A><SPAN class="verseno">8 </SPAN>This is why that field was called "Field of Blood." <I>It was still called that</I> until the day <I>that Matthew wrote this</I>.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:9"></A><SPAN class="verseno">9 </SPAN>Then what God stated through the preacher Jeremiah was accomplished. He said, "And they took the thirty silver coins (the amount they had priced one of Israel's sons),</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:10"></A><SPAN class="verseno">10 </SPAN>and they gave these for the clay worker's field aligned with what the Master dictated to me" <I>(Zechariah 11:12-13)</I>.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:11"></A><SPAN class="verseno">11 </SPAN><I>The soldiers</I> stood Jesus up in front of the Roman leader, and the leader asked Him, "Are You the Jewish people's king?" "You are saying it," declared Jesus.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:12"></A><SPAN class="verseno">12 </SPAN>The head priests and older men leveled many complaints against Him, but He answered nothing.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:13"></A><SPAN class="verseno">13 </SPAN>At that time, Pilate told Him, "Don't You hear how many things they are saying they witnessed against You?"</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:14"></A><SPAN class="verseno">14 </SPAN>He didn't respond with even one statement. This really amazed the leader.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:15"></A><SPAN class="verseno">15 </SPAN>At each festival, the leader was accustomed to dismissing one prisoner, whoever the crowd wanted.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:16"></A><SPAN class="verseno">16 </SPAN>At that time, Barabbas was a well-known prisoner.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:17"></A><SPAN class="verseno">17 </SPAN>So since a crowd had gathered, Pilate told them, "Who do you want me to dismiss? Barabbas or Jesus, the One called Anointed King?"</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:18"></A><SPAN class="verseno">18 </SPAN>You see, he realized that the Jewish leaders turned Him in because they were jealous of Him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:19"></A><SPAN class="verseno">19 </SPAN>As he was seated at the judicial bench, his wife sent out <I>this message</I> to him: "Don't do anything to that Person who does what is right. You see, I suffered much today in a dream because of Him."</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:20"></A><SPAN class="verseno">20 </SPAN>But the head priests and the older men persuaded the crowds to ask that Barabbas be released and Jesus be ruined.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:21"></A><SPAN class="verseno">21 </SPAN>When the leader responded, he said, "Which of the two do you want me to dismiss?" The crowds said, "Barabbas."</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:22"></A><SPAN class="verseno">22 </SPAN>"So what should I do with Jesus," says Pilate, "the One who is called Anointed King?" Everyone says, "He must be nailed to a cross."</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:23"></A><SPAN class="verseno">23 </SPAN>But the leader was saying, "You see, what did He do that was bad?" They were yelling even louder, "He must be nailed to a cross."</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:24"></A><SPAN class="verseno">24 </SPAN>When Pilate sees he is not helping the situation but instead a riot is starting, he ends up taking some water. He washed off his hands up in front of the crowd and said, "I am not guilty of this Man's blood. <I>It is your problem.</I> You will see <I>to it</I>."</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:25"></A><SPAN class="verseno">25 </SPAN>When the entire group responded, they said, "His blood is on us and on our children."</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:26"></A><SPAN class="verseno">26 </SPAN>At that time, he dismissed Barabbas. But he thrashed Jesus with the Roman whip and turned Him over <I>to the soldiers</I> so that they would nail Him to a cross.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:27"></A><SPAN class="verseno">27 </SPAN>Then the leader's soldiers took Jesus into the Roman palace and gathered the whole regiment together.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:28"></A><SPAN class="verseno">28 </SPAN>After they stripped Him, they put a red military cape around Him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:29"></A><SPAN class="verseno">29 </SPAN>They wove an award wreath out of thorns and put it on His head. They put a stick in His right hand. Then they kneeled in front of Him and mocked Him. "Happy to meet You, King of the Jewish people," they said.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:30"></A><SPAN class="verseno">30 </SPAN>They spit on Him, took the stick, and were hitting Him on the head.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:31"></A><SPAN class="verseno">31 </SPAN>When they were done mocking Him, they stripped the military cape off of Him and put His clothes back on. Then they led Him out to be nailed to a cross.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:32"></A><SPAN class="verseno">32 </SPAN>As they came out, they found a Cyrenian man named Simon. They sequestered help from this man so that he might pick up His cross.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:33"></A><SPAN class="verseno">33 </SPAN>They went to a place called Golgotha which means "Place of a Skull."</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:34"></A><SPAN class="verseno">34 </SPAN>They gave Him wine mixed with bile to drink. When He tasted it, He didn't want to drink it.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:35"></A><SPAN class="verseno">35 </SPAN>After they nailed Him to a cross, they divided up His clothes by throwing dice.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:36"></A><SPAN class="verseno">36 </SPAN>Then they sat down and were keeping guard of Him there.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:37"></A><SPAN class="verseno">37 </SPAN>They placed His accusation up above His head. <I>This was what</I> had been written, "This is Jesus, the Jewish people's king."</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:38"></A><SPAN class="verseno">38 </SPAN>At that time, two bandits were also nailed to crosses, one to the right of Him and one to the left.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:39"></A><SPAN class="verseno">39 </SPAN>As people traveled by there, they were insulting Him and shaking their heads.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:40"></A><SPAN class="verseno">40 </SPAN>"The One who tears the temple down and builds it in three days," they were saying, "rescue Yourself if You are a son of God, and climb down off the cross."</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:41"></A><SPAN class="verseno">41 </SPAN>The head priests were also mocking Him with the Old Testament transcribers and the older men in the same way.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:42"></A><SPAN class="verseno">42 </SPAN>"Others, He rescued," they were saying, "Himself, He can't rescue. Isn't He the King of Israel? He must climb down off the cross now, and we will trust Him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:43"></A><SPAN class="verseno">43 </SPAN>He has been so sure about God. God must save Him now, if He wants Him. You see, He said, 'I am a son of a god.'"</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:44"></A><SPAN class="verseno">44 </SPAN>The bandits, the ones nailed to crosses together with Him, were also criticizing Him in the same way.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:45"></A><SPAN class="verseno">45 </SPAN>At noon, it became dark over all the earth and stayed dark until 3 p.m.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:46"></A><SPAN class="verseno">46 </SPAN>Around 3 p.m. Jesus shouted loudly, "Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani?" That is <I>Aramaic for</I> "My God, My God, why did You abandon Me?"</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:47"></A><SPAN class="verseno">47 </SPAN>When some of the people standing there heard it, they were saying, "This Person is hollering for Elijah."</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:48"></A><SPAN class="verseno">48 </SPAN>Right away, one person from them ran, took a sponge, filled it with sour wine, put it around a stick, and gave Him a drink.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:49"></A><SPAN class="verseno">49 </SPAN>"Leave Him alone," everyone else said. "Let's see if Elijah comes to rescue Him."</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:50"></A><SPAN class="verseno">50 </SPAN>Jesus let out a loud yell again and let the spirit go <I>(in other words, He died)</I>.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:51"></A><SPAN class="verseno">51 </SPAN>And, look, the temple's curtain tore in two from top to bottom, the earth shook, rocks tore apart,</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:52"></A><SPAN class="verseno">52 </SPAN>burial vaults opened, and many sacred people's bodies that had fallen asleep got up.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:53"></A><SPAN class="verseno">53 </SPAN>(They didn't come out of the cemetery until after Jesus came back to life. At that time, they went into the sacred city and explicitly showed themselves to many.)</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:54"></A><SPAN class="verseno">54 </SPAN>When the lieutenant and the soldiers with him (who were keeping guard of Jesus) saw the earthquake and what happened, they were terribly afraid. "This truly was a son of a god," they said.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:55"></A><SPAN class="verseno">55 </SPAN>Many women were there watching off at a distance. These were the ones that followed Jesus from Galilee and served Him,</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:56"></A><SPAN class="verseno">56 </SPAN>Mary (the Magdalene), Mary (the mother of James and Joseph), and the mother of Zebedee's sons were among them.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:57"></A><SPAN class="verseno">57 </SPAN>In the evening, a wealthy man from Arimathaea named Joseph showed up. He was a student of Jesus.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:58"></A><SPAN class="verseno">58 </SPAN>He had gone to Pilate and asked for Jesus' body. At that time, Pilate had ordered <I>his soldiers</I> to give <I>the body</I> back to him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:59"></A><SPAN class="verseno">59 </SPAN>Joseph took the body, wound a clean linen cloth around it,</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:60"></A><SPAN class="verseno">60 </SPAN>and put it in his new burial vault that he had chiseled out of rock. He rolled a large stone over the doorway of the burial vault and left.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:61"></A><SPAN class="verseno">61 </SPAN>Mary (the Magdalene) and the other Mary were there sitting up in front of the gravesite.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:62"></A><SPAN class="verseno">62 </SPAN>The next day, the day that is after the <I>Festival's</I> preparation day, the head priests and the Separatists were gathered together facing Pilate.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:63"></A><SPAN class="verseno">63 </SPAN>"Master," they said, "we remembered that while that misleader was still alive, He said that He would be gotten up after three days.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:64"></A><SPAN class="verseno">64 </SPAN>So order <I>your soldiers</I> to secure the gravesite until the third day <I>is over</I>. That way His students won't ever go and steal His body, then tell the group that He was gotten up from the dead. If that happens, the last misleading scheme will be worse than the first."</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:65"></A><SPAN class="verseno">65 </SPAN>"You have a Roman guard unit," Pilate declared. "Lead the way back there, and secure the gravesite however you think <I>it should be secured</I>."</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 27:66"></A><SPAN class="verseno">66 </SPAN>The head priests traveled over to the gravesite and secured it by putting a seal on the stone in the presence of the Roman guard unit.</P>
<TITLE>Matthew 28</TITLE>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 28:1"></A><SPAN class="verseno">1 </SPAN>The evening of the Sabbaths, as it was emerging into Day One <I>(which is Sunday)</I> after the Sabbaths, Mary (the Magdalene) and the other Mary went to watch the gravesite.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 28:2"></A><SPAN class="verseno">2 </SPAN>And look, there was a large earthquake. You see, after the Master's angel stepped down from heaven and went to the gravesite, he rolled the stone away and was sitting up on top of it.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 28:3"></A><SPAN class="verseno">3 </SPAN>He looked like lightning, and his attire was white as snow.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 28:4"></A><SPAN class="verseno">4 </SPAN>The soldiers who were keeping guard <I>of the tomb</I> shook with fear and became as dead people.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 28:5"></A><SPAN class="verseno">5 </SPAN>When the angel responded, he told the women, "You must not be afraid. You see, I realize that you are looking for Jesus, the One who has been nailed to a cross.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 28:6"></A><SPAN class="verseno">6 </SPAN>He isn't here. You see, God got Him up, just as Jesus said He would. Come. Look at the place where He was lying.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 28:7"></A><SPAN class="verseno">7 </SPAN>And travel quickly and tell His students that God got Him up from the dead and that, look, He is leading the way ahead of you into Galilee. You will see Him there. Look, I told you."</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 28:8"></A><SPAN class="verseno">8 </SPAN>They quickly left the burial vault with fear and great happiness and ran to report it to His students.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 28:9"></A><SPAN class="verseno">9 </SPAN>And look, Jesus came to meet them. "Happy to see you," He said. The women came forward, took hold of His feet, and bowed down to Him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 28:10"></A><SPAN class="verseno">10 </SPAN>"Don't be afraid," said Jesus. "Make your way back. Report to My brothers that I will go off into Galilee and they will see Me there."</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 28:11"></A><SPAN class="verseno">11 </SPAN>As they were traveling off, look, some of the Roman guard unit went into the city and reported absolutely everything to the head priests.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 28:12"></A><SPAN class="verseno">12 </SPAN>The head priests gathered with the older men and received counsel <I>on what to do</I>. They decided to give an adequate amount of silver coins to the soldiers</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 28:13"></A><SPAN class="verseno">13 </SPAN>and tell them, "Say that His students came at night and stole Him as you were sleeping.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 28:14"></A><SPAN class="verseno">14 </SPAN>If the leader hears this, we will persuade him and make it so that you have nothing to worry about."</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 28:15"></A><SPAN class="verseno">15 </SPAN>The soldiers took the silver coins and did as they were told. This message <I>(that His students stole His body)</I> was thoroughly spread beside the Jewish people up to the day <I>that Matthew wrote this book</I>.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 28:16"></A><SPAN class="verseno">16 </SPAN>The eleven students traveled into Galilee to the mountain that Jesus previously arranged with them.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 28:17"></A><SPAN class="verseno">17 </SPAN>When they saw Him, they bowed down. But the people doubted <I>that it was really Jesus</I>.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 28:18"></A><SPAN class="verseno">18 </SPAN>Jesus went and spoke to them. "All authority in heaven and on earth was given to Me.</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 28:19"></A><SPAN class="verseno">19 </SPAN>So after traveling, make students of all the nations. Submerge them in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Sacred Spirit,</P>
<P><A NAME="Matthew 28:20"></A><SPAN class="verseno">20 </SPAN>and teach them to keep all the things that I demanded you. And look, I will be with you everyday until the very conclusion of the span of time.</P>
<TITLE>Mark 1</TITLE>
<P><A NAME="Mark 1:1"></A><SPAN class="verseno">1 </SPAN>Here is the beginning of the good news of Jesus, the Anointed King, God's Son.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 1:2"></A><SPAN class="verseno">2 </SPAN>The preacher Isaiah wrote about it. "Look, I am sending My messenger out on a mission before Your face. He will construct Your road" <I>(Malachi 3:1)</I>.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 1:3"></A><SPAN class="verseno">3 </SPAN>"A voice is shouting in the backcountry, 'Get the Master's road ready. Make His paths straight'" <I>(Isaiah 40:3)</I>.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 1:4"></A><SPAN class="verseno">4 </SPAN>John started submerging people in the backcountry. He was speaking in public about a change-of-ways submersion for forgiveness of sins. <I>Submersion is a Jewish tradition that ritually cleans the person being submerged.</I></P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 1:5"></A><SPAN class="verseno">5 </SPAN>All kinds of people from the rural area (Judea) and the Jerusalemites were traveling out to him. He was submerging them in the Jordan River after they admitted their sins out loud.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 1:6"></A><SPAN class="verseno">6 </SPAN>John put on <I>the same kind of clothes that Elijah and some old-time preachers wore:</I> clothes made of camel hair and a leather strap around his waist. He ate grasshoppers and wild honey.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 1:7"></A><SPAN class="verseno">7 </SPAN>When he was speaking publicly, he also was saying, "The One who is stronger than me is coming behind me. I am unfit to stoop and untie His sandals' straps.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 1:8"></A><SPAN class="verseno">8 </SPAN>I submerged you in water, but He will submerge you in the Sacred Spirit."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 1:9"></A><SPAN class="verseno">9 </SPAN>In those days, Jesus came from Nazareth, Galilee and was submerged by John in the Jordan <I>River</I>.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 1:10"></A><SPAN class="verseno">10 </SPAN>As He stepped up from the water, right away He saw the skies torn open. The Spirit came down to Him as a dove.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 1:11"></A><SPAN class="verseno">11 </SPAN>A voice came from the sky: "You are My loved Son. I am delighted with You."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 1:12"></A><SPAN class="verseno">12 </SPAN>Right away the Spirit threw Him out into the backcountry.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 1:13"></A><SPAN class="verseno">13 </SPAN>He was in the backcountry forty days being harassed by the Opponent. He was with wild animals, and angels were serving Him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 1:14"></A><SPAN class="verseno">14 </SPAN>After John had been taken into custody, Jesus went into Galilee speaking publicly about God's good news.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 1:15"></A><SPAN class="verseno">15 </SPAN>"The appointed time has come," He said, "and God's monarchy has come near. Change your ways, and trust in the good news."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 1:16"></A><SPAN class="verseno">16 </SPAN>As He was passing along the Sea of Galilee, He saw Simon and Simon's brother (Andrew) throwing <I>a net</I> in the sea on both <I>sides of the boat</I>. You see, they were fishermen.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 1:17"></A><SPAN class="verseno">17 </SPAN>"Come on behind Me," Jesus told them, "and I will make you into fishermen of people."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 1:18"></A><SPAN class="verseno">18 </SPAN>Right away they left their nets and followed Him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 1:19"></A><SPAN class="verseno">19 </SPAN>He walked on a little further and saw James (Zebedee's son) and James' brother (John) as they were in their boat mending the nets.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 1:20"></A><SPAN class="verseno">20 </SPAN>Right away He invited them. They left their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired workers and went off behind Him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 1:21"></A><SPAN class="verseno">21 </SPAN>They traveled into Capernaum. Right away on the Sabbaths, He went into the synagogue and taught.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 1:22"></A><SPAN class="verseno">22 </SPAN>They were impressed with His teaching. You see, He was teaching them as someone with authority would <I>(as a king or a master would teach the people under him)</I>. This was not how the Old Testament transcribers taught.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 1:23"></A><SPAN class="verseno">23 </SPAN>Right away in their synagogue, there was a person who had a spirit that was not clean. The spirit yelled out.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 1:24"></A><SPAN class="verseno">24 </SPAN>It said, "Jesus, Nazarene, why are You interfering with us? Did You come to ruin us? I realize who You are, God's Sacred One."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 1:25"></A><SPAN class="verseno">25 </SPAN>Jesus stopped it, "Be quiet, and come out of him," He said.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 1:26"></A><SPAN class="verseno">26 </SPAN>The spirit that wasn't clean sent him into convulsions, hollered loudly, and came out of him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 1:27"></A><SPAN class="verseno">27 </SPAN>Absolutely everyone was so perplexed that together they were posing questions to each other, "What is this new <I>way of</I> teaching <I>with authority?</I> He even gives orders to spirits that aren't clean and they obey Him."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 1:28"></A><SPAN class="verseno">28 </SPAN>Right away, talk about Him went out everywhere into the whole surrounding rural area of Galilee.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 1:29"></A><SPAN class="verseno">29 </SPAN>They left the synagogue and right away went into Simon and Andrew's house with James and John.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 1:30"></A><SPAN class="verseno">30 </SPAN>Simon's mother-in-law was lying down with a fever. Right away they told Jesus about her.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 1:31"></A><SPAN class="verseno">31 </SPAN>He went to her, took her hand, and got her up. Her fever left. She served them.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 1:32"></A><SPAN class="verseno">32 </SPAN>In the evening, after the sun set, they were bringing everyone to Him that had something wrong with them and the ones that had lesser deities.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 1:33"></A><SPAN class="verseno">33 </SPAN>The whole city had come together to one place facing the door.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 1:34"></A><SPAN class="verseno">34 </SPAN>He healed many people who had something wrong <I>with them, who had</I> various illnesses, and threw out many lesser deities. He wasn't allowing the lesser deities to speak because they knew Him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 1:35"></A><SPAN class="verseno">35 </SPAN>In the morning while it was still very dark, He got up, left <I>the house</I>, went off to an uninhabited place, and was praying there.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 1:36"></A><SPAN class="verseno">36 </SPAN>Simon and the people with him hunted Him down.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 1:37"></A><SPAN class="verseno">37 </SPAN>When Simon found Him, he told Him, "Everyone is looking for You."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 1:38"></A><SPAN class="verseno">38 </SPAN>"Let's take some other way into the next towns," He said, "so that I may speak in public there too. You see, this is why I came out."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 1:39"></A><SPAN class="verseno">39 </SPAN>He went into their synagogues in all of Galilee speaking publicly and throwing out the lesser deities.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 1:40"></A><SPAN class="verseno">40 </SPAN>A man with a skin disease comes up to Him urging Him and kneeling. "If You want to, You are able to clear my skin up," he said.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 1:41"></A><SPAN class="verseno">41 </SPAN>Jesus had sympathy on him. He put out His hand, touched him, and told him, "I want to. Be cleared up."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 1:42"></A><SPAN class="verseno">42 </SPAN>Right away the skin disease went away from him, and he was cleared up.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 1:43"></A><SPAN class="verseno">43 </SPAN>After being stern with him, right away, Jesus threw him out.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 1:44"></A><SPAN class="verseno">44 </SPAN>"Look, don't tell anyone anything," He said. "But make your way back to the priest, show yourself to him, and for the clearing up of your skin disease go through <I>the eight day process</I> stipulated by Moses <I>in Leviticus 14</I>. That will be a witness to them <I>of what happened to you.</I>"</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 1:45"></A><SPAN class="verseno">45 </SPAN>But when the man left, he began speaking in public often and thoroughly spreading the message <I>of what happened to him</I>. <I>He did this</I> so much that Jesus was no longer able to go into a city without hiding Himself. Instead He was outside in uninhabited places, and people were coming to Him from all directions.</P>
<TITLE>Mark 2</TITLE>
<P><A NAME="Mark 2:1"></A><SPAN class="verseno">1 </SPAN>After a few days, He went into Capernaum again. People heard that He was in a certain house,</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 2:2"></A><SPAN class="verseno">2 </SPAN>and many gathered there. There were so many people that there wasn't room for even one more, not even around the door. He was speaking to them about the message.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 2:3"></A><SPAN class="verseno">3 </SPAN>Some people came bringing a disabled man to Him. Four of them carried him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 2:4"></A><SPAN class="verseno">4 </SPAN>Since they couldn't get to Him because of the crowd, they removed the roof above where He was. After digging it out, they lowered the mattress <I>through the hole</I> with the disabled man lying down on it.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 2:5"></A><SPAN class="verseno">5 </SPAN>When Jesus saw their trust, He said to the disabled man, "Child, your sins are forgiven."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 2:6"></A><SPAN class="verseno">6 </SPAN>Some Old Testament transcribers were sitting there and pondering in their hearts:</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 2:7"></A><SPAN class="verseno">7 </SPAN>"Why is this Person speaking like this? He is insulting God. <I>It is obvious that God crippled this man because of some terrible sins.</I> Who can forgive <I>those</I> sins? Only One, God."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 2:8"></A><SPAN class="verseno">8 </SPAN>When Jesus correctly understood with His spirit that this is what they were pondering, right away He told them, "Why are you pondering these things in your hearts?</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 2:9"></A><SPAN class="verseno">9 </SPAN>Which is easier to say to the disabled man, 'Your sins are forgiven,' or, 'Get up, pick up your mattress, and walk around?'</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 2:10"></A><SPAN class="verseno">10 </SPAN>But so that you may realize that the Son of the Person has authority to be forgiving sins on the earth...." He told the disabled man,</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 2:11"></A><SPAN class="verseno">11 </SPAN>"I tell you, get up, pick up your mattress, and make your way back to your house."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 2:12"></A><SPAN class="verseno">12 </SPAN>Right away He got up, picked up his mattress, and went out in front of everyone. Everyone was astounded and praised the magnificence of God. "We have never ever seen anything like this," they said.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 2:13"></A><SPAN class="verseno">13 </SPAN>Jesus went out along the sea again. The entire crowd was coming to Him, and He was teaching them.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 2:14"></A><SPAN class="verseno">14 </SPAN>As He passed by the tax booth, He saw Levi (Alphaeus' son) sitting there. "Follow Me," He told him. Levi got up and followed Him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 2:15"></A><SPAN class="verseno">15 </SPAN>After that, Jesus happened to be lounging in Levi's house. Many tax collectors and sinful people were feasting and chatting together with Jesus and His students. You see, there were many of them, and they were following Him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 2:16"></A><SPAN class="verseno">16 </SPAN>When the Separatists' Old Testament transcribers saw that He was eating with sinful people and tax collectors, they were saying to His students, "He is eating with tax collectors and sinful people."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 2:17"></A><SPAN class="verseno">17 </SPAN>When Jesus heard it, He told them, "The people who are healthy and well don't need a doctor, but the people who have something wrong with them do. I didn't come to invite people who do what is right <I>to live for God</I>. I came to invite sinful people."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 2:18"></A><SPAN class="verseno">18 </SPAN>John's students and the Separatists' students were abstaining from eating. They came and said to Him, "Why do John's students and the Separatists' students abstain from eating, but Your students don't?"</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 2:19"></A><SPAN class="verseno">19 </SPAN>Jesus told them, "The 'sons of the bridal room' <I>(the people negotiating with the groom for the bride and helping her with the wedding)</I> can't abstain from eating while the groom is with them, can they? <I>No, eating is a big part of the negotiation process and the wedding.</I> As long as the groom is there with them, they can't be abstaining from eating.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 2:20"></A><SPAN class="verseno">20 </SPAN>But days will come when the groom is gone, then they will be able to abstain from eating.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 2:21"></A><SPAN class="verseno">21 </SPAN>No one sews a patch of unprocessed cloth on a well-worn robe. <I>If they do that,</I> the <I>patch</I> that fills in <I>the hole</I> lifts away from it, the new from the well-worn, and the tear becomes worse.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 2:22"></A><SPAN class="verseno">22 </SPAN>And no one puts wine that is in the early stages of fermentation into worn-out leather bags. If they were to do that, the wine would rip the leather bags open, and the wine and the leather bags would be ruined. But they put wine that is in the early stages of fermentation into new leather bags."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 2:23"></A><SPAN class="verseno">23 </SPAN>He happened to be traveling along through the croplands on the Sabbaths. His students began pulling the heads of grain off the plants along the way.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 2:24"></A><SPAN class="verseno">24 </SPAN>"Look," the Separatists said to Him, "what they are doing <I>is work. Why are they working</I> on the Sabbaths? That is not allowed."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 2:25"></A><SPAN class="verseno">25 </SPAN>"Have you never even once read," He asked them, "what David and the people with him did when they had a need and were hungry?</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 2:26"></A><SPAN class="verseno">26 </SPAN><I>Haven't you read</I> how David went into God's house based on the head priest Abiathar's <I>approval</I>, ate the display bread (that no one is allowed to eat except the priests), and also gave it to the people with him? <I>Do you condemn David for doing that? No.</I>"</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 2:27"></A><SPAN class="verseno">27 </SPAN>"God made the Sabbath for people," He told them. "He didn't make people for the Sabbath.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 2:28"></A><SPAN class="verseno">28 </SPAN>In this way, the Son of the Person is also the Sabbath's master." <I>("The Son of the Person" is a generic term Jesus used of Himself. Ezekiel and Daniel were called "son of a person." "Son of a person" is also in Psalm 80:17.)</I></P>
<TITLE>Mark 3</TITLE>
<P><A NAME="Mark 3:1"></A><SPAN class="verseno">1 </SPAN>He went into the synagogue again, and a man was there whose hand was shriveled up.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 3:2"></A><SPAN class="verseno">2 </SPAN>They were watching Him closely to see if He would heal him on the Sabbaths so that they might level a complaint against Him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 3:3"></A><SPAN class="verseno">3 </SPAN>He told the man with the shriveled up hand, "Get up in the middle <I>of the room</I>."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 3:4"></A><SPAN class="verseno">4 </SPAN>Then He turned to the people. "Which is allowed on the Sabbath?" He asked, "To do something good for this man or to do something bad? To rescue a soul or to kill?" But they were silent.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 3:5"></A><SPAN class="verseno">5 </SPAN>After He looked around at them with rage, He was saddened by the hardness of their hearts. "Put out your hand," He told the man. He put out his hand, and it was established back <I>to normal</I>.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 3:6"></A><SPAN class="verseno">6 </SPAN>Right away the Separatists and the Herod supporters left. They took counsel against Him on how they might ruin Him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 3:7"></A><SPAN class="verseno">7 </SPAN>Jesus took a back way to the sea with His students. A very large number of people followed Him. They were from Galilee, Judea,</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 3:8"></A><SPAN class="verseno">8 </SPAN>Greater Jerusalem, Idumaea, the other side of the Jordan <I>River</I>, and the area around Tyre and Sidon. Large amounts of people were hearing about all the things that He was doing. As they heard, they came to Him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 3:9"></A><SPAN class="verseno">9 </SPAN>He told His students to have a small boat close by because of the crowd so that they wouldn't give Him a hard time.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 3:10"></A><SPAN class="verseno">10 </SPAN>You see, He healed so many that they were falling on Him. As many as had ailments were trying to touch Him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 3:11"></A><SPAN class="verseno">11 </SPAN>And whenever the spirits that were not clean saw Him, they were falling toward Him and yelling, "You are the Son of God."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 3:12"></A><SPAN class="verseno">12 </SPAN>He was shushing many <I>spirits</I> in them so that they wouldn't show who He is.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 3:13"></A><SPAN class="verseno">13 </SPAN>He climbed up a mountain. <I>From there,</I> He called for people He was wanting, and they went off to Him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 3:14"></A><SPAN class="verseno">14 </SPAN>From these, He made up a group of twelve that He also called missionaries so that they would be with Him and He could send them out on missions to speak publicly</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 3:15"></A><SPAN class="verseno">15 </SPAN>and to have the authority to throw out lesser deities. The Twelve were</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 3:16"></A><SPAN class="verseno">16 </SPAN>Simon (He gave him the name, Peter <I>or Rock</I>),</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 3:17"></A><SPAN class="verseno">17 </SPAN>James (Zebedee's son), John (James' brother; He also gave these brothers the name, Boanerges, which is <I>Hebrew for</I> Sons of Thunder),</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 3:18"></A><SPAN class="verseno">18 </SPAN>Andrew, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Thomas, James (Alphaeus' son), Thaddeus, Simon (the Zealot),</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 3:19"></A><SPAN class="verseno">19 </SPAN>and Judas from Kerioth (who also turned Him in). He went into a house,</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 3:20"></A><SPAN class="verseno">20 </SPAN>and the crowd came together again in such a way for them not to be able to even eat bread.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 3:21"></A><SPAN class="verseno">21 </SPAN>When the people <I>who lived</I> beside Him heard about this, they went out to take Him into custody. You see, they were saying that He is deranged.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 3:22"></A><SPAN class="verseno">22 </SPAN>Old Testament transcribers walked down out of Greater Jerusalem to where He was. They were saying that He has Beelzebub in Him and that is how He throws lesser deities out since Beelzebub is the head of the lesser deities.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 3:23"></A><SPAN class="verseno">23 </SPAN>After calling for them, He was telling them in illustrations, "How is the Opponent able to be throwing the Opponent out?</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 3:24"></A><SPAN class="verseno">24 </SPAN>If a monarchy is divided and disagrees with itself, that monarchy cannot be established.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 3:25"></A><SPAN class="verseno">25 </SPAN>And if a house is divided and disagrees with itself, that house won't be able to be established.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 3:26"></A><SPAN class="verseno">26 </SPAN>And if the Opponent stands up against himself and is divided, he can't stand. That would be the conclusion of him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 3:27"></A><SPAN class="verseno">27 </SPAN><I>So I am not throwing out lesser deities with Beelzebub. But I am throwing them out.</I> No one is able to go into a strong person's house <I>while he is there</I> and ransack his stuff unless he first ties him up. Then he can ransack his house.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 3:28"></A><SPAN class="verseno">28 </SPAN>Amen, I tell you that everything will be forgiven to the sons of people, the sins and the insults, however many things they might insult.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 3:29"></A><SPAN class="verseno">29 </SPAN>But whoever insults into the Sacred Spirit doesn't have forgiveness for the span of time. He is eligible for sentencing on sin that spans all time."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 3:30"></A><SPAN class="verseno">30 </SPAN>He said this because they were saying that He has a spirit that is not clean.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 3:31"></A><SPAN class="verseno">31 </SPAN>His mother and brothers came to where He was. As they stood outside, they sent someone out on a mission <I>to go in and</I> get Him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 3:32"></A><SPAN class="verseno">32 </SPAN>Inside, a crowd was sitting around Him. They told Him, "Look, Your mother, brothers, and sisters are outside looking for You."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 3:33"></A><SPAN class="verseno">33 </SPAN>When He answered them, He said, "Who is My mother and brothers?"</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 3:34"></A><SPAN class="verseno">34 </SPAN>After looking around at the people sitting in a circle around Him, He said, "Look, My mother and My brothers.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 3:35"></A><SPAN class="verseno">35 </SPAN>You see, whoever does what God wants is My brother, sister, and mother."</P>
<TITLE>Mark 4</TITLE>
<P><A NAME="Mark 4:1"></A><SPAN class="verseno">1 </SPAN>Again He began to teach beside the Sea <I>of Galilee</I>, and the biggest crowd gathered. He climbed on board a boat and sat in it so that He could sit and be in the sea. The whole crowd was on the land facing the sea.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 4:2"></A><SPAN class="verseno">2 </SPAN>He was teaching them many things in illustrations. In His teaching, He said,</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 4:3"></A><SPAN class="verseno">3 </SPAN>"Listen. Look. The person who plants crops went out to plant. <I>His method of planting was flinging handfuls of seeds out on the ground throughout the whole field.</I></P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 4:4"></A><SPAN class="verseno">4 </SPAN>As he was flinging seeds, <I>one</I> happened to fall along the road, and birds came and ate it.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 4:5"></A><SPAN class="verseno">5 </SPAN>Another <I>seed</I> fell on the rocky part where there wasn't much soil. Right away it sprang up because the soil didn't have any depth.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 4:6"></A><SPAN class="verseno">6 </SPAN>When the sun came up, it got hot, and because it didn't have roots, it dried up.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 4:7"></A><SPAN class="verseno">7 </SPAN>Another <I>seed</I> fell in thorns. The thorns climbed up, came together, and choked it out. It didn't give any fruit.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 4:8"></A><SPAN class="verseno">8 </SPAN><I>There were</I> others. <I>This group</I> fell into nice soil and was giving fruit. It climbed up, grew, and was having fruit: one thirty, one sixty, and one a hundred."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 4:9"></A><SPAN class="verseno">9 </SPAN>He was also saying, "The person who has ears for listening must listen."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 4:10"></A><SPAN class="verseno">10 </SPAN>When He was alone <I>taking a break</I>, the people around Him together with the Twelve asked Him about the illustrations.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 4:11"></A><SPAN class="verseno">11 </SPAN>"The secret of God's monarchy," He told them, "has been given to you, but to those outside, everything is in illustrations.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 4:12"></A><SPAN class="verseno">12 </SPAN>That way as they look, they can look and not see, and as they hear, they can hear and not understand. They'll never return back and be forgiven."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 4:13"></A><SPAN class="verseno">13 </SPAN>"Don't you know what this illustration shows?" He said. "How will you know all the illustrations?</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 4:14"></A><SPAN class="verseno">14 </SPAN><I>This illustration shows the different responses people have when they hear God's message.</I> The person who flings out <I>the seeds</I> flings out the message.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 4:15"></A><SPAN class="verseno">15 </SPAN><I>When some people hear the message, they reject it.</I> These are the ones where the seed of the message falls along the road. When they hear it, right away, the Opponent comes and takes the message away that has been planted in them..</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 4:16"></A><SPAN class="verseno">16 </SPAN><I>When other people hear the message, they accept it for a while.</I> These are the ones that are flung on the rocky parts. When they hear the message, right away, they receive the message and are happy about it.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 4:17"></A><SPAN class="verseno">17 </SPAN>But the message doesn't have any root in them. It is for the time being. After that, when there are hard times or persecution, right away they stumble.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 4:18"></A><SPAN class="verseno">18 </SPAN>Others are like when the seeds are flung into the thorns. These hear the message,</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 4:19"></A><SPAN class="verseno">19 </SPAN>but worry <I>about the things that happen in this</I> span of time, the fraud of wealth, and desires for the other things travel in. These come together and choke off the message. It becomes fruitless.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 4:20"></A><SPAN class="verseno">20 </SPAN>Others are like when the seeds are flung on the nice soil. They hear the message and warmly welcome it. They produce fruit: one thirty, one sixty, and one a hundred."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 4:21"></A><SPAN class="verseno">21 </SPAN>He was also telling them, "A lamp doesn't come into a room to be placed under the two gallon measuring basket or under the cot, does it? No, it comes into a room to be placed up high on a stand.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 4:22"></A><SPAN class="verseno">22 </SPAN>You see, something is not hidden if it can't ever be shown. Someone hides something away so that someday it might be shown.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 4:23"></A><SPAN class="verseno">23 </SPAN>If anyone has ears for listening, he must listen."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 4:24"></A><SPAN class="verseno">24 </SPAN>He was also telling them, "Watch what kind of things you listen to. The amount that you measure out will be measured to you and added to you.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 4:25"></A><SPAN class="verseno">25 </SPAN>You see, the person who has will get. And the person who doesn't have, even what he has will be taken away from him."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 4:26"></A><SPAN class="verseno">26 </SPAN>He was also saying, "God's monarchy is like this, like a person who threw a batch of seeds on the ground.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 4:27"></A><SPAN class="verseno">27 </SPAN>Day and night he slept and got up. The batch of seeds budded and grew taller. How? He doesn't know.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 4:28"></A><SPAN class="verseno">28 </SPAN>The earth automatically produces fruit: first a stem, after that a head of grain, then full grain in the head of grain.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 4:29"></A><SPAN class="verseno">29 </SPAN>But when the fruit turned up, right away he sent out the sickle <I>to harvest it</I> because the harvest had offered itself to him."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 4:30"></A><SPAN class="verseno">30 </SPAN>He was also saying, "How will we show what God's monarchy is like? Or in what illustration will we put it?</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 4:31"></A><SPAN class="verseno">31 </SPAN>It is as a mustard kernel, that, when it is planted in the earth, it is littler than all <I>kinds of</I> seeds on the earth.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 4:32"></A><SPAN class="verseno">32 </SPAN>Yet whenever it is planted, it climbs up and becomes greater than all <I>kinds of</I> vegetables. It makes large branches so that the birds of the sky can nest under its shadow."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 4:33"></A><SPAN class="verseno">33 </SPAN>He was speaking the message to them with many of these types of illustrations, just what they were able to hear.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 4:34"></A><SPAN class="verseno">34 </SPAN>He wasn't speaking to them without an illustration. But He explained everything to His students when they were by themselves.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 4:35"></A><SPAN class="verseno">35 </SPAN>When evening came that day, He told them, "We will go across to the other side."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 4:36"></A><SPAN class="verseno">36 </SPAN>They left the crowd and took Him along in the boat since He was already in it. There were other boats with them.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 4:37"></A><SPAN class="verseno">37 </SPAN>A large blast of wind came. It was throwing the swells up into the boat in such a way for the boat to already be full of water.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 4:38"></A><SPAN class="verseno">38 </SPAN>He was in the back of the boat on the cushion sleeping. They got Him up and said, "Teacher, aren't you concerned that we are getting destroyed?"</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 4:39"></A><SPAN class="verseno">39 </SPAN>When He was wide awake, He shushed the wind and told the sea, "Silence. Be quiet." The wind stopped blowing, and it became very calm.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 4:40"></A><SPAN class="verseno">40 </SPAN>"Why are you cowards?" He asked them. "Don't you have trust yet?"</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 4:41"></A><SPAN class="verseno">41 </SPAN>They feared great fear. "So who is this?" they were saying to each other, "because even the wind and the sea obey Him?"</P>
<TITLE>Mark 5</TITLE>
<P><A NAME="Mark 5:1"></A><SPAN class="verseno">1 </SPAN>They went to the other side <I>(the eastern side)</I> of the Sea <I>of Galilee</I> to the rural area of the Gerasenes.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 5:2"></A><SPAN class="verseno">2 </SPAN>When He came out of the boat, right away a man who had a spirit that was not clean came to Him from the cemetery.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 5:3"></A><SPAN class="verseno">3 </SPAN>He was living in the cemetery. No one could chain him up anymore</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 5:4"></A><SPAN class="verseno">4 </SPAN>because he had been locked up many times with foot shackles and chains, but he pulled the chains apart and crushed the foot shackles. No one was strong enough to tame him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 5:5"></A><SPAN class="verseno">5 </SPAN>Through it all, night and day, he was yelling and cutting himself with stones in the graves and in the mountains.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 5:6"></A><SPAN class="verseno">6 </SPAN>When he had seen Jesus off at a distance, he ran and bowed down to Him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 5:7"></A><SPAN class="verseno">7 </SPAN>He let out a loud yell and said, "What are You here for, Jesus, son of God, the Highest? I place you under an oath with God not to torture me."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 5:8"></A><SPAN class="verseno">8 </SPAN>You see, Jesus was telling it, "You, the spirit that is not clean, come out of the man."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 5:9"></A><SPAN class="verseno">9 </SPAN>He also was asking it, "What is your name?" "My name is Legion," it said, "because there are many of us. <I>(Legion is the Latin word for regiment.)</I></P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 5:10"></A><SPAN class="verseno">10 </SPAN>And it was urging Him much to not send them outside of the rural area.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 5:11"></A><SPAN class="verseno">11 </SPAN>A large herd of hogs were there toward the mountain, grazing.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 5:12"></A><SPAN class="verseno">12 </SPAN>"Send us into the hogs," they urged Him, "so that we might go into them."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 5:13"></A><SPAN class="verseno">13 </SPAN>He gave them permission to go. When the spirits that were not clean came out, they went into the hogs, and the herd of about two thousand hogs rushed down the steep slope into the sea. There they drowned.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 5:14"></A><SPAN class="verseno">14 </SPAN>The people grazing them escaped <I>from the stampede</I> into the fields and the city. There they reported what had happened. The people from the fields and the city came to see it.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 5:15"></A><SPAN class="verseno">15 </SPAN>They are coming to Jesus and watching the man who has the lesser deities. The man who had the legion is sitting, clothed and sane. They were afraid.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 5:16"></A><SPAN class="verseno">16 </SPAN>Those who had seen what happened to the man and the hogs described it all to them.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 5:17"></A><SPAN class="verseno">17 </SPAN>They began to urge Him to leave their border area.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 5:18"></A><SPAN class="verseno">18 </SPAN>As He was climbing on board the boat, the man who had the lesser deities was urging Jesus to let him come along.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 5:19"></A><SPAN class="verseno">19 </SPAN>He didn't let him. Instead, He told him, "Make your way back to your people into your house, and report to them how much the Master has done for you and that He showed you forgiving kindness."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 5:20"></A><SPAN class="verseno">20 </SPAN>He went away and began speaking publicly in Decapolis about how much Jesus had done for him. Everyone was amazed.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 5:21"></A><SPAN class="verseno">21 </SPAN>After Jesus crossed all the way back over <I>the Sea of Galilee</I> in the boat, a big crowd gathered to hear Him. He again was beside the sea.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 5:22"></A><SPAN class="verseno">22 </SPAN>One of the synagogue's head rulers with the name Jairus came. When he saw Jesus, he got down on the ground facing His feet</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 5:23"></A><SPAN class="verseno">23 </SPAN>and urged Him much. "My little daughter is dying," he said. "Please come and place Your hands on her so that she might be rescued and live."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 5:24"></A><SPAN class="verseno">24 </SPAN>Jesus went off with him. A big crowd was following Him and squeezing in on Him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 5:25"></A><SPAN class="verseno">25 </SPAN>There was a woman who had been bleeding for twelve years.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 5:26"></A><SPAN class="verseno">26 </SPAN>She had suffered through many treatments from many doctors and spent everything she had, but she was not any better. Instead, she was getting worse.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 5:27"></A><SPAN class="verseno">27 </SPAN>When she heard about Jesus, she came up from behind in the crowd and touched His robe.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 5:28"></A><SPAN class="verseno">28 </SPAN>You see, she was telling herself, "If I just touch His robe, I will be rescued <I>from this bleeding</I>."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 5:29"></A><SPAN class="verseno">29 </SPAN>Right away the spring of her blood dried up, and she knew in her body that she had been cured from the ailment.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 5:30"></A><SPAN class="verseno">30 </SPAN>Right away Jesus recognized in Himself that <I>some type of</I> ability had gone out of Him. He turned around in the crowd. "Who touched My robe?" He said.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 5:31"></A><SPAN class="verseno">31 </SPAN>His students told Him, "You see how the crowd is squeezing in on You. How are You saying, 'Who touched Me?'"</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 5:32"></A><SPAN class="verseno">32 </SPAN>He was looking around trying to see who did it.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 5:33"></A><SPAN class="verseno">33 </SPAN>But the woman, who had been afraid and was trembling, realized what had happened to her. She came, got down <I>on the ground</I> facing Him, and told Him the whole truth.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 5:34"></A><SPAN class="verseno">34 </SPAN>"Daughter, your trust has rescued you," Jesus told her. "Make your way back home in peace and be well from your ailment."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 5:35"></A><SPAN class="verseno">35 </SPAN>As He was still speaking, people from the head ruler's house came. "Your daughter died," they said. "Why irritate the teacher anymore?"</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 5:36"></A><SPAN class="verseno">36 </SPAN>When Jesus overheard the message, He told the head ruler, "Don't be afraid. Just trust."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 5:37"></A><SPAN class="verseno">37 </SPAN>He only allowed Peter, James, and John (James' brother) to follow along with Him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 5:38"></A><SPAN class="verseno">38 </SPAN>They went into the head ruler's house. He watched the disturbance caused by people crying and clanging things.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 5:39"></A><SPAN class="verseno">39 </SPAN>He went into the room and said, "Why are you causing a disturbance and crying? The young child isn't dead. She's sleeping."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 5:40"></A><SPAN class="verseno">40 </SPAN>They were laughing at Him. He threw everyone out. He took the father, the mother, and the <I>three</I> along with Him and traveled into where the young child was.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 5:41"></A><SPAN class="verseno">41 </SPAN>He took hold of the young child's hand and told her, "Talitha Cumi," which is <I>Aramaic</I> and translated as "Girl, I tell you, get up."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 5:42"></A><SPAN class="verseno">42 </SPAN>Right away the girl got up and started walking around. You see, she was twelve years old. They were immediately astounded with great astonishment.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 5:43"></A><SPAN class="verseno">43 </SPAN>He warned them much not to let anyone know about this and told them to give her something to eat.</P>
<TITLE>Mark 6</TITLE>
<P><A NAME="Mark 6:1"></A><SPAN class="verseno">1 </SPAN>He left there and went to His hometown. His students followed Him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 6:2"></A><SPAN class="verseno">2 </SPAN>When the Sabbath came, He began to teach in the synagogue, and many listening were impressed. "Where does this Man get these things from?" they said. "What is the insight that has been given to this Man? What are these types of abilities that His hands do?</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 6:3"></A><SPAN class="verseno">3 </SPAN>Isn't this the builder? Isn't He Mary's son? Isn't He the brother of James, Joses <I>(Joseph)</I>, Judah <I>(Jude)</I>, and Simon? Aren't His sisters living here with us?" They were stumbling on Him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 6:4"></A><SPAN class="verseno">4 </SPAN>"A preacher is only worthless," Jesus told them, "in his hometown, among his relatives, and in his house."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 6:5"></A><SPAN class="verseno">5 </SPAN>He wasn't able to show even one of His abilities there, except that He placed His hands on a few sick people and healed them.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 6:6"></A><SPAN class="verseno">6 </SPAN>He was amazed at their lack of trust and was taking His students around to the circling villages, teaching.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 6:7"></A><SPAN class="verseno">7 </SPAN>He called for the Twelve and began to send them out on missions, two by two. He gave them authority over the spirits that are not clean.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 6:8"></A><SPAN class="verseno">8 </SPAN>He ordered them not to take anything for the road except a staff: no bread, no tote bag, no copper in their money belts <I>(copper was used as money)</I>.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 6:9"></A><SPAN class="verseno">9 </SPAN>"But put some shoes on and don't put on two shirts," He also told them.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 6:10"></A><SPAN class="verseno">10 </SPAN>"Whenever you go into a house, stay there until you leave that village.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 6:11"></A><SPAN class="verseno">11 </SPAN>If a place doesn't accept you or listen to you, as you travel out from there, shake off the dirt beneath your feet for a witness to them. <I>Don't tell them they are wrong. Don't argue with them. Just shake off the dirt. That is enough.</I></P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 6:12"></A><SPAN class="verseno">12 </SPAN>They went out to the places where Jesus sent them and spoke publicly telling them to change their ways.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 6:13"></A><SPAN class="verseno">13 </SPAN>They threw many lesser deities out, dabbed olive oil on many sick people, and healed them.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 6:14"></A><SPAN class="verseno">14 </SPAN>King Herod heard about it. You see, <I>Jesus'</I> name became well known. "The John who submerges," he said, "has come back to life from the dead. That's why the abilities are active in Him."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 6:15"></A><SPAN class="verseno">15 </SPAN>But others were saying, "He is Elijah," and others, "He is a preacher who is like one of the preachers <I>in the Bible</I>."</P>

<P><A NAME="Mark 9:1"></A><SPAN class="verseno">1 </SPAN>He was telling them, "Amen, I tell you that some people standing here will not in any way taste death until they see God's monarchy come in its ability."</P>

<P><A NAME="Mark 9:4"></A><SPAN class="verseno">4 </SPAN>They saw Elijah together with Moses and they were speaking together with Jesus.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 9:5"></A><SPAN class="verseno">5 </SPAN>"Rabbi," responded Peter, "it is nice for us to be here. Let's make three tents: one for You, one for Moses, and one for Elijah."</P>
