<P><A NAME="Mark 12:8"></A><SPAN class="verseno">8 </SPAN>They took him, killed him, and threw his body out of the vineyard.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 12:9"></A><SPAN class="verseno">9 </SPAN>So what will the vineyard's master do? He will come, ruin the farmers, and give the vineyard to others.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 12:10"></A><SPAN class="verseno">10 </SPAN>Didn't you ever read this <I>Old Testament</I> writing? 'A stone that the builders rejected has ended up being used for a corner's head, <I>(a cornerstone, the primary stone of the whole building)</I>.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 12:11"></A><SPAN class="verseno">11 </SPAN>This came directly from the Master, and it is amazing in our eyes' <I>(Psalm 118:22-23)</I>."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 12:12"></A><SPAN class="verseno">12 </SPAN>They were looking for a way to take Him into custody, and yet they were cautious of the crowd. You see, they knew that He told the illustration specifically for them. Then they left Him alone and went away.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 12:13"></A><SPAN class="verseno">13 </SPAN>But they were sending some of the Separatists and the Herod Supporters out to Him so that they might catch Him in the answers He gave them.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 12:14"></A><SPAN class="verseno">14 </SPAN>They came and told Him, "Teacher, we realize that You are valid and there is no bias in You toward anyone. You see, You don't look at people's labels, but You teach the way of God based on truth. Is it permitted to give an enrollment tax to Caesar or not?</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 12:15"></A><SPAN class="verseno">15 </SPAN>Should we give or not give?" But Jesus realized that their behavior was fake. "Why are you harassing Me?" He told them. "Bring Me a denarius <I>(a coin equal to one day's wage)</I> so that I might see it."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 12:16"></A><SPAN class="verseno">16 </SPAN>They brought Him one. "Whose image and inscription is this?" He asked. "Caesar's," they said.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 12:17"></A><SPAN class="verseno">17 </SPAN>"Give Caesar's things back to Caesar and God's things back to God," Jesus told them. They were amazed.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 12:18"></A><SPAN class="verseno">18 </SPAN>Sadducees came to Him. The Sadducees say that there is no life after death. They were asking <I>Him a question</I>.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 12:19"></A><SPAN class="verseno">19 </SPAN>"Teacher," they said, "Moses wrote to us that if someone dies and leaves a wife behind without a child, that his brother should take the wife and bring up a seed <I>(descendants)</I> for his brother.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 12:20"></A><SPAN class="verseno">20 </SPAN>There were seven brothers. After the first took a wife, he died and didn't leave a seed <I>(he didn't have any children)</I>.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 12:21"></A><SPAN class="verseno">21 </SPAN>The second took her and died without leaving a seed behind either. The same thing happened with the third.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 12:22"></A><SPAN class="verseno">22 </SPAN>The seven brothers didn't leave a seed <I>(descendants)</I>. Last of all, the wife also died.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 12:23"></A><SPAN class="verseno">23 </SPAN>In the return back to life when they come back to life, whose wife will she be? You see, all seven had her as a wife."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 12:24"></A><SPAN class="verseno">24 </SPAN>"Aren't you misled," declared Jesus, "because you don't know the <I>Old Testament</I> writings or God's ability?</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 12:25"></A><SPAN class="verseno">25 </SPAN>You see, whenever they come back to life from the dead, they don't marry and they don't plan to get married either. They are like the angels in heaven.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 12:26"></A><SPAN class="verseno">26 </SPAN>But about the dead coming back to life, haven't you read in Moses' scroll, how God said to him at the bush, 'I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob <I>(Exodus 3:6)?' He didn't say 'was'. He said 'am'. I am the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.</I></P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 12:27"></A><SPAN class="verseno">27 </SPAN>God is not a god of dead people. <I>Dead people don't have gods. They are dead.</I> He is a god of living people. <I>Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob were and are living in the afterworld.</I> You are misled about many things."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 12:28"></A><SPAN class="verseno">28 </SPAN>One of the Old Testament transcribers came forward. He had listened to them together posing questions to Him and had seen that He answered them nicely. He asked Him, "Which is the first demand of all?"</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 12:29"></A><SPAN class="verseno">29 </SPAN>Jesus answered, "First is, 'Listen, Israel, the Master, our God, is One Master,</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 12:30"></A><SPAN class="verseno">30 </SPAN>and you will love the Master, your God, from your whole heart, from your whole soul, from your whole mind, and from your whole strength.'</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 12:31"></A><SPAN class="verseno">31 </SPAN>Second is this, 'You will love the person near you as yourself.' There is no other demand greater than these."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 12:32"></A><SPAN class="verseno">32 </SPAN>"Teacher, You answered nicely based on truth," the Old Testament transcriber told Him, "because there is One, and there is not another other than Him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 12:33"></A><SPAN class="verseno">33 </SPAN>And to love Him from the whole heart, from the whole understanding, and from the whole strength, and to love the person nearby as oneself is even more than all the entirely burned offerings and sacrifices."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 12:34"></A><SPAN class="verseno">34 </SPAN>When Jesus saw that he answered thoughtfully, He told him, "You are not a long way away from God's monarchy." No one dared to ask Him anything anymore.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 12:35"></A><SPAN class="verseno">35 </SPAN>Jesus responded by saying this as He taught on the temple grounds: "How do the Old Testament transcribers say that the Anointed King is a son of David?</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 12:36"></A><SPAN class="verseno">36 </SPAN>David himself said in the Sacred Spirit, 'The Master <I>(God)</I> said to my Master <I>(the Anointed King)</I>, Sit down on My right side until I place Your enemies beneath Your feet' <I>(Psalm 110:1)</I>.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 12:37"></A><SPAN class="verseno">37 </SPAN>David himself called Him Master. How is He his son?" The large crowd was gladly listening to Him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 12:38"></A><SPAN class="verseno">38 </SPAN>In His teaching He was saying, "Look out for the Old Testament transcribers who want to walk around in long robes, who want people to greet them in the marketplace,</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 12:39"></A><SPAN class="verseno">39 </SPAN>who want the front benches in the synagogues and the front reclining places <I>(the place of honor)</I> in the feasts,</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 12:40"></A><SPAN class="verseno">40 </SPAN>who eat up widows' houses, and who pray long prayers for a sham. They will receive much more judgment."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 12:41"></A><SPAN class="verseno">41 </SPAN>When He was seated directly facing the treasury area, He was watching how the crowd threw copper coins into <I>the collection boxes in</I> the treasury area. Many wealthy people were throwing in much.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 12:42"></A><SPAN class="verseno">42 </SPAN>One poor widow came and threw in two tiny brass coins worth a penny.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 12:43"></A><SPAN class="verseno">43 </SPAN>He called for His students and told them, "Amen, I tell you that this poor widow threw more into the treasury area than anyone else.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 12:44"></A><SPAN class="verseno">44 </SPAN>You see, everyone threw in part of what they had left over, but she, even though she didn't make enough to live on, threw in everything, as much as she had, her whole life savings."</P>
<TITLE>Mark 13</TITLE>
<P><A NAME="Mark 13:1"></A><SPAN class="verseno">1 </SPAN>As He was traveling out of the temple grounds, one of His students told Him, "Teacher, look! What stones! And what buildings!"</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 13:2"></A><SPAN class="verseno">2 </SPAN>"Do you see these large buildings?" Jesus told him. "Here a stone will not in any way be left on a stone that hasn't been torn down."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 13:3"></A><SPAN class="verseno">3 </SPAN>As He sat on the Mount of Olives directly facing the temple grounds, Peter, James, John, and Andrew were by themselves with Him. They were asking Him,</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 13:4"></A><SPAN class="verseno">4 </SPAN>"Tell us. When will these things be? And what will indicate when everything is about to be completely finished?"</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 13:5"></A><SPAN class="verseno">5 </SPAN>Jesus began by saying, "See that no one misleads you.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 13:6"></A><SPAN class="verseno">6 </SPAN>Many will come using My name and saying, 'I am Him.' They will mislead many.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 13:7"></A><SPAN class="verseno">7 </SPAN>When you hear wars and much talk about wars, do not be alarmed. This must happen, but it is not the conclusion yet.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 13:8"></A><SPAN class="verseno">8 </SPAN>You see, a nation will rise up against a nation and a monarchy against a monarchy. There will be earthquakes throughout some areas. There will be famines. These are the beginning of labor pains.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 13:9"></A><SPAN class="verseno">9 </SPAN>You all must look at yourselves. Some of your own people will turn you in to councils. You will be beaten in synagogues. You will stand before leaders and kings on account of Me for a witness to them.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 13:10"></A><SPAN class="verseno">10 </SPAN>First, it is necessary for the good news to be spoken publicly to all the nations.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 13:11"></A><SPAN class="verseno">11 </SPAN>Whenever they turn you in and take you away, don't worry beforehand about what you should speak, but speak whatever is given to you in that hour. You see, you are not the ones speaking, the Sacred Spirit is.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 13:12"></A><SPAN class="verseno">12 </SPAN>A brother will turn a brother in to be put to death; and a father, a child. Children will stand up against parents and put them to death.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 13:13"></A><SPAN class="verseno">13 </SPAN>You will be hated by everyone because of My name, but whoever persists to do what is right to the conclusion, this person will be rescued.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 13:14"></A><SPAN class="verseno">14 </SPAN>The disgusting thing of the uninhabited time will stand where it must not stand. The person reading <I>about this in Daniel</I> must be aware of it. When you see that this has happened, at that time the people in Judea must escape into the mountains.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 13:15"></A><SPAN class="verseno">15 </SPAN>The person on top of the house must not first climb down into the house or go in to take anything from his house.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 13:16"></A><SPAN class="verseno">16 </SPAN>The person in the field must not first return back to his stuff to take his robe. <I>Escape immediately.</I></P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 13:17"></A><SPAN class="verseno">17 </SPAN>What a tragedy it will be for the pregnant women and the nursing women in those days.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 13:18"></A><SPAN class="verseno">18 </SPAN>Be praying so that your escape will not happen during a storm.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 13:19"></A><SPAN class="verseno">19 </SPAN>You see, those days will be hard times. That kind of <I>hard times</I> has not in anyway happened since the beginning of the creation that God created until now and will not in anyway happen <I>after that</I>.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 13:20"></A><SPAN class="verseno">20 </SPAN>If the Master didn't halt those days, no physical body would be rescued. But God halted those days because of the select people, <I>the people</I> who selected Him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 13:21"></A><SPAN class="verseno">21 </SPAN>At that time, if someone tells you, 'Look, the Anointed King is here, look He's over there,' don't trust it.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 13:22"></A><SPAN class="verseno">22 </SPAN>You see, counterfeit anointed kings and counterfeit preachers will get up and give proofs and incredible things with a specific goal--to mislead away <I>from God</I>, if possible, the people who have selected God.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 13:23"></A><SPAN class="verseno">23 </SPAN>You must look out <I>for these things</I>. I have stated it all to you beforehand.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 13:24"></A><SPAN class="verseno">24 </SPAN>In those days, after the hard times, the sun will darken, the moon won't give its glow,</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 13:25"></A><SPAN class="verseno">25 </SPAN>stars will fall out of the sky, and heaven's abilities will be disturbed.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 13:26"></A><SPAN class="verseno">26 </SPAN>Then they will see the Son of the Person coming in clouds with much ability and magnificence.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 13:27"></A><SPAN class="verseno">27 </SPAN>Then He will send the angels out and bring the people who selected Him together in one place from the four winds <I>(the four compass directions)</I>, from the edge of the earth to the edge of heaven.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 13:28"></A><SPAN class="verseno">28 </SPAN>Learn this illustration from the fig tree. Whenever its branch already becomes tender and it sprouts the leaves out, you know that summer is near.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 13:29"></A><SPAN class="verseno">29 </SPAN>In this way also, whenever you see these things happening, know that it is near, at the door.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 13:30"></A><SPAN class="verseno">30 </SPAN>Amen, I tell you that a generation will not in any way pass by until all these things happen <I>(from their beginning until the day He comes)</I>.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 13:31"></A><SPAN class="verseno">31 </SPAN>The sky and the earth will pass, but My messages will not in any way pass.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 13:32"></A><SPAN class="verseno">32 </SPAN>No one except the Father knows the day or hour <I>of His coming</I>, not the angels in heaven, not the Son.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 13:33"></A><SPAN class="verseno">33 </SPAN>Look for <I>these things</I>! Don't go to sleep! You see, you don't know when the appointed time is.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 13:34"></A><SPAN class="verseno">34 </SPAN><I>It is</I> like a man who left his house to go out of town. He gave his authority to his slaves. Each was to be responsible for his own work, and he gave a demand to the doorkeeper to stay awake.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 13:35"></A><SPAN class="verseno">35 </SPAN>In the same way, you also must stay awake. You see, you don't know when the house's master is coming: either evening, or middle of the night, or rooster-crowing time <I>(3-6 a.m.)</I>, or in the morning.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 13:36"></A><SPAN class="verseno">36 </SPAN>When he comes unexpectedly, he won't find you sleeping, will he?</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 13:37"></A><SPAN class="verseno">37 </SPAN>What I say to you, I say to everyone, stay awake."</P>
<TITLE>Mark 14</TITLE>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:1"></A><SPAN class="verseno">1 </SPAN>The Passover and the Yeast-free Festival was two days away. The head priests and the Old Testament transcribers were looking for a way to kill Him once they took Him into custody using deception.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:2"></A><SPAN class="verseno">2 </SPAN>You see, they were saying, "Not at the festival so that there won't be a riot among the ethnic group."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:3"></A><SPAN class="verseno">3 </SPAN>As He was in Bethany lounging in the house of Simon (the man with a skin disease), a woman came with an alabaster jar of very expensive authentic Spikenard perfume. After she crushed the alabaster jar, she spilled it down on His head.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:4"></A><SPAN class="verseno">4 </SPAN>Some of them were frustrated at this. "Why would she ruin this perfume?" they said to each other.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:5"></A><SPAN class="verseno">5 </SPAN>"You see, this perfume could have been put up for sale for over three hundred denarii <I>($15,000)</I>, and that could have been given to the poor." They were stern with her.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:6"></A><SPAN class="verseno">6 </SPAN>"Leave her alone," said Jesus. "Why are you bothering her? She has worked to do nice work for Me.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:7"></A><SPAN class="verseno">7 </SPAN>You see, you always have the poor with you. Whenever you want, you can do something good for them. But you won't always have Me.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:8"></A><SPAN class="verseno">8 </SPAN>She did this because this is what she had. She brought it early to perfume My body for its embalming.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:9"></A><SPAN class="verseno">9 </SPAN>Amen, I tell you, wherever the good news is spoken publicly in the whole world, what she did will also be spoken for a reminder of her."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:10"></A><SPAN class="verseno">10 </SPAN>Judas (from Kerioth, one of the Twelve) went off to the head priests so that he might turn Him in to them.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:11"></A><SPAN class="verseno">11 </SPAN>When the head priests heard, they were happy and promised to give him silver. He was looking for a way to turn Him in.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:12"></A><SPAN class="verseno">12 </SPAN>For the first day of the Yeast-free Festival (when they sacrifice the Passover lamb), His students said to Him, "Where do You want us to go off to and get things ready for eating the Passover meal?"</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:13"></A><SPAN class="verseno">13 </SPAN>He sent two of His students out. "Make your way back into the city," He told them, "and a person hauling a clay pitcher of water will meet you. Follow him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:14"></A><SPAN class="verseno">14 </SPAN>Wherever he enters, tell the homeowner, 'The teacher says, "Where is My guest room? I need a place to eat the Passover meal with My students."'</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:15"></A><SPAN class="verseno">15 </SPAN>He will show you a large room above the ground floor that has been set up and is ready. Get things ready for us there."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:16"></A><SPAN class="verseno">16 </SPAN>The students left, went into the city, and found just what He told them. They got the Passover meal ready.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:17"></A><SPAN class="verseno">17 </SPAN>When evening arrived, He came with the Twelve.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:18"></A><SPAN class="verseno">18 </SPAN>As they reclined and ate, Jesus said, "Amen, I tell you that one person from among you will turn Me in, the one eating with Me."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:19"></A><SPAN class="verseno">19 </SPAN>They began to be sad and to be saying to Him, one by one, "It isn't me, is it?"</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:20"></A><SPAN class="verseno">20 </SPAN>"It is one of the Twelve," He told them, "the one dipping <I>bread</I> into the bowl with Me.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:21"></A><SPAN class="verseno">21 </SPAN>The Son of the Person certainly makes His way back just as the Bible says, but what a tragedy it is to that person through whom the Son of the Person is turned in. It would have been nice for that person if he had not been born."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:22"></A><SPAN class="verseno">22 </SPAN>As they were eating, He took bread, conferred a blessing on it, split it, and gave it to them. "Take it," He said. "This is My body."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:23"></A><SPAN class="verseno">23 </SPAN>When He took a cup, after being thankful, He gave it to them, and everyone drank from it.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:24"></A><SPAN class="verseno">24 </SPAN>"This is My blood of the deal," He told them, "the blood that is spilled out on behalf of many.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:25"></A><SPAN class="verseno">25 </SPAN>Amen, I tell you that I won't in any way drink juice from a grapevine anymore until that day, whenever I drink it new in God's monarchy."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:26"></A><SPAN class="verseno">26 </SPAN>After they sang praise songs, they went out to the Mount of Olives.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:27"></A><SPAN class="verseno">27 </SPAN>"All of you will stumble," Jesus told them, "because the Bible says, 'I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will disperse' <I>(Zechariah 13:7)</I>.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:28"></A><SPAN class="verseno">28 </SPAN>But after I am gotten up, I will lead the way ahead of you into Galilee."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:29"></A><SPAN class="verseno">29 </SPAN>But Peter was declaring to Him, "Even if all of them stumble, I won't."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:30"></A><SPAN class="verseno">30 </SPAN>"Amen, I tell you," Jesus told him, "that you, today, on this night, before it is time for a rooster to even crow twice, you will flatly deny Me three times."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:31"></A><SPAN class="verseno">31 </SPAN>But Peter was insisting even more, "If I have to die together with You, I will not in any way flatly deny You." They all were also saying this.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:32"></A><SPAN class="verseno">32 </SPAN>They came into a parcel of land. Its name is Gethsemane <I>(Aramaic for oil press)</I>. "Be seated here while I pray," He told His students.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:33"></A><SPAN class="verseno">33 </SPAN>Then He took Peter, James, and John along with Him. He began to be puzzled and heavyhearted.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:34"></A><SPAN class="verseno">34 </SPAN>"My soul is overcome with sadness to death," He told them. "Stay here and stay awake."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:35"></A><SPAN class="verseno">35 </SPAN>After He went on ahead a little, He was getting down on the ground and praying that, if it is possible, the hour <I>(the events that were about to happen)</I> might go away.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:36"></A><SPAN class="verseno">36 </SPAN>This is what He was saying: "Daddy, the Father, all things are possible for You. Carry this cup off away from Me. But not what I want. What You want."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:37"></A><SPAN class="verseno">37 </SPAN>He came and found them sleeping. "Simon, are you sleeping?" He asked Peter. "Didn't you have enough strength to stay awake one hour?</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:38"></A><SPAN class="verseno">38 </SPAN>Stay awake and pray so that you won't get into trouble. The spirit certainly is eager, but the physical body is weak."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:39"></A><SPAN class="verseno">39 </SPAN>He went off again and prayed the same words.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:40"></A><SPAN class="verseno">40 </SPAN>Again He came and found them sleeping. You see, their eyes were weighted down a lot, and they didn't know how to respond to Him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:41"></A><SPAN class="verseno">41 </SPAN>When He came the third time, He told them, "Sleep for the rest of the time, and relax. He has it all." <I>Later, He said,</I> "The hour has come. Look, the Son of the Person is being turned over to sinful people's hands.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:42"></A><SPAN class="verseno">42 </SPAN>Get up. Let's lead the way. Look, the person turning Me in has come near."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:43"></A><SPAN class="verseno">43 </SPAN>Right away as He was still speaking, Judas, one of the Twelve, showed up. With him was a crowd carrying daggers and wooden clubs. They had come directly from the head priests, the Old Testament transcribers, and the older men.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:44"></A><SPAN class="verseno">44 </SPAN>Judas had given them a signal. "Whoever I am friendly with is Him," he told them. "Take Him into custody and lead Him away securely."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:45"></A><SPAN class="verseno">45 </SPAN>When he came, right away he went up to Jesus and said, "Rabbi." He was very friendly to Him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:46"></A><SPAN class="verseno">46 </SPAN>They put their hands on Him and took Him into custody.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:47"></A><SPAN class="verseno">47 </SPAN>A certain student standing nearby, pulled out his dagger, struck the head priest's slave, and took off his earlobe.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:48"></A><SPAN class="verseno">48 </SPAN>"You came out to apprehend Me," responded Jesus, "with daggers and wooden clubs as if I were a bandit.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:49"></A><SPAN class="verseno">49 </SPAN>I was facing you on the temple grounds throughout the day teaching, and you didn't take Me into custody. But this is so that what the <I>Old Testament</I> writings say might be accomplished."</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:50"></A><SPAN class="verseno">50 </SPAN>All of His students left and ran away.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:51"></A><SPAN class="verseno">51 </SPAN>One of them was a certain young lad. He had been following Jesus having put only a linen cloth around himself over his naked body. They grabbed him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:52"></A><SPAN class="verseno">52 </SPAN>But he left the linen cloth with them and escaped naked.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:53"></A><SPAN class="verseno">53 </SPAN>They led Jesus off to the head priest. All the head priests, older men, and Old Testament transcribers came together.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:54"></A><SPAN class="verseno">54 </SPAN>Peter followed Him off at a distance until He was inside, in the courtyard of the head priest. There Peter was sitting together with the underlings and warming himself facing the light.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:55"></A><SPAN class="verseno">55 </SPAN>The head priests and the whole council were looking for <I>something that</I> a witness <I>had seen Jesus do</I> which they could put Him to death for, but they weren't finding anything.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:56"></A><SPAN class="verseno">56 </SPAN>You see, many were lying about what they actually witnessed, and the witness accounts didn't match up.</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:57"></A><SPAN class="verseno">57 </SPAN>Some stood up and were lying as they said,</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:58"></A><SPAN class="verseno">58 </SPAN>"We heard Him say, 'I will tear this handmade temple down and in three days build another one made without hands.'"</P>
<P><A NAME="Mark 14:59"></A><SPAN class="verseno">59 </SPAN>But even their accounts about this didn't match up.</P>

<P><A NAME="Luke 4:17"></A><SPAN class="verseno">17 </SPAN>A scroll of the preacher Isaiah was given to Him. He unrolled it and found the place where it has been written:</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 4:18"></A><SPAN class="verseno">18 </SPAN>"The Master's Spirit is on Me. Because of this, He anointed Me to share good news with the poor. He has sent Me out on a mission to speak publicly about forgiveness to incarcerated people and about sight restoration to blind people, to send shattered people out in forgiveness,</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 4:19"></A><SPAN class="verseno">19 </SPAN>and to speak publicly about the Master's acceptance year" <I>(Isaiah 61:1-2). The acceptance year is a time when God accepts all who come to Him.</I></P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 4:20"></A><SPAN class="verseno">20 </SPAN>He rolled up the scroll, gave it back to the underling, and sat down. All the eyes in the synagogue were staring at Him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 4:21"></A><SPAN class="verseno">21 </SPAN>He began speaking to them, "Today, what this writing says will happen has been accomplished in your ears."</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 4:22"></A><SPAN class="verseno">22 </SPAN>All were telling what they had seen Him do. They kept being amazed at the messages about God's generosity traveling out of His mouth. "Is this not a son of Joseph?" they were saying.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 4:23"></A><SPAN class="verseno">23 </SPAN>"By all means," He told them, "you will state this proverb to Me, 'Doctor, heal yourself <I>with the remedies that you prescribe to others</I>.' As many <I>miracles</I> as we heard about happening in Capernaum, do them here in your hometown too."</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 4:24"></A><SPAN class="verseno">24 </SPAN>He also said, "Amen, I tell you that not even one preacher is accepted in his hometown.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 4:25"></A><SPAN class="verseno">25 </SPAN>But I tell you. It is true. There were many widows in Israel in Elijah's days when he closed the sky for three and a half years causing a large famine over the entire earth.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 4:26"></A><SPAN class="verseno">26 </SPAN>Elijah was not even sent in the direction of any of them, but into <I>a small foreign town</I> (Sarepta of the Sidonian <I>territory</I>) to a <I>foreign</I> woman, a widow.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 4:27"></A><SPAN class="verseno">27 </SPAN>And there were many people with a skin disease in Israel when Elisha was the preacher. Not even one of them was cleared up, but a Syrian (Naaman) was. <I>Why does God have to go to outsiders to find someone deserving of His blessing?</I></P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 4:28"></A><SPAN class="verseno">28 </SPAN>Everyone in the synagogue was filled with anger when they heard these things.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 4:29"></A><SPAN class="verseno">29 </SPAN>They stood up, threw Him out of the city, and took Him up to an overhang of the mountain on which their city was built so that they could throw Him down the steep slope.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 4:30"></A><SPAN class="verseno">30 </SPAN>But He went through the middle of them and was traveling off.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 4:31"></A><SPAN class="verseno">31 </SPAN>He went down to Capernaum, a city of Galilee, and was teaching them on the Sabbaths.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 4:32"></A><SPAN class="verseno">32 </SPAN>They were impressed with His teaching because His message was with authority. <I>He was teaching like a king or master would.</I></P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 4:33"></A><SPAN class="verseno">33 </SPAN>In the synagogue, there was a person who had a lesser deity's spirit, a spirit that was not clean. It yelled out with a loud voice,</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 4:34"></A><SPAN class="verseno">34 </SPAN>"Ahhhh! Jesus, Nazarene, why are You interfering with us? Did you come to ruin us? I know who You are, God's Sacred One."</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 4:35"></A><SPAN class="verseno">35 </SPAN>Jesus stopped him by saying, "Be quiet and come out of him." The lesser deity tossed him into the middle of the synagogue and came out without hurting him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 4:36"></A><SPAN class="verseno">36 </SPAN>Everyone was perplexed. They were speaking together to each other, saying, "What is this answer <I>that He gave to the lesser deity?</I> He gives orders with authority and ability to spirits that are not clean and they come out."</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 4:37"></A><SPAN class="verseno">37 </SPAN>Talk about Him was echoing around and traveling out into every place in the surrounding rural area.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 4:38"></A><SPAN class="verseno">38 </SPAN>He got up out of the synagogue and went into Simon's house. Simon's mother-in-law was constrained by a high fever. So they asked Him about her.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 4:39"></A><SPAN class="verseno">39 </SPAN>When He stood up above her, He told the fever to stop, and it left her. At once, she stood up and started serving them.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 4:40"></A><SPAN class="verseno">40 </SPAN>As the sun was setting, absolutely everyone brought Him as many people as they had who were in frail health with various illnesses. Jesus was placing His hands on each one of them and healing them.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 4:41"></A><SPAN class="verseno">41 </SPAN>Lesser deities were also coming out of many, yelling, "You are the Son of God." He was shushing them, not allowing them to speak because they knew that He was the Anointed King.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 4:42"></A><SPAN class="verseno">42 </SPAN>In the morning at the crack of dawn, He left and traveled into an uninhabited place. The crowds started looking for Him and went everywhere until they found Him. They were delaying Him so that He wouldn't travel somewhere else.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 4:43"></A><SPAN class="verseno">43 </SPAN>"I must share the good news of God's monarchy with different cities too," He told them, "because that's what I was sent out to do."</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 4:44"></A><SPAN class="verseno">44 </SPAN>He was speaking publicly in the synagogues of Judea.</P>
<TITLE>Luke 5</TITLE>
<P><A NAME="Luke 5:1"></A><SPAN class="verseno">1 </SPAN>There was a time when the crowd was leaning on Jesus and listening to God's message. He happened to be standing beside Lake Gennesaret <I>(which is another name for the Sea of Galilee)</I>.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 5:2"></A><SPAN class="verseno">2 </SPAN>He saw two boats sitting along the side of the lake. The fishermen had stepped out of them to rinse the nets.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 5:3"></A><SPAN class="verseno">3 </SPAN>He climbed on board one of the boats (Simon's) and asked him to take Him out a little bit away from the land. When he was seated, He was teaching the crowds from the boat.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 5:4"></A><SPAN class="verseno">4 </SPAN>When He was done speaking, He told Simon, "Take us out where it is deep and lower your nets for a catch."</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 5:5"></A><SPAN class="verseno">5 </SPAN>"Boss, we have labored through the whole night," responded Simon, "and taken nothing. But based on Your statement, I will lower the nets."</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 5:6"></A><SPAN class="verseno">6 </SPAN>When they did this, they captured a very large number of fish. Their nets were ripping apart.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 5:7"></A><SPAN class="verseno">7 </SPAN>They motioned to their teammates in a different boat so that they would come and bring them in together. They came and filled both boats so full that they were sinking down <I>into the water</I>.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 5:8"></A><SPAN class="verseno">8 </SPAN>After Simon Peter saw it, he got down at Jesus' knees and said, "Go out away from me because I am a sinful man, Master."</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 5:9"></A><SPAN class="verseno">9 </SPAN>You see, he and the others with him were very perplexed about the catch of fish that together they had taken.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 5:10"></A><SPAN class="verseno">10 </SPAN>Likewise, James and John (Zebedee's sons) were also <I>very perplexed</I>. They were partners with Simon. "Don't be afraid," Jesus told Simon. "From now on, you will be catching people alive."</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 5:11"></A><SPAN class="verseno">11 </SPAN>After they brought the boats up on land, they left everything and followed Him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 5:12"></A><SPAN class="verseno">12 </SPAN>There was a time when He happened to be in one of the cities, and look, a man with a skin disease all over his body was there. When he saw Jesus, he got down on his face and pleaded with Him, "Master, if you want to, you can clear my skin up."</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 5:13"></A><SPAN class="verseno">13 </SPAN>He put out His hand and touched him. "I want to," He said. "Be cleared up." Right away the skin disease went away from him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 5:14"></A><SPAN class="verseno">14 </SPAN>Jesus ordered him not to tell anyone. "When you leave, show yourself to the priest," Jesus said, "and for the clearing up of your skin disease go through <I>the eight day process</I> just as it was stipulated by Moses <I>in Leviticus 14</I>. That will be a witness to them <I>of what happened to you.</I>"</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 5:15"></A><SPAN class="verseno">15 </SPAN>But the message about Jesus was going through there even more. Large crowds were coming together to listen to Him and to be healed from their frailties.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 5:16"></A><SPAN class="verseno">16 </SPAN>When He could, He was slipping away secretly to the uninhabited places and praying.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 5:17"></A><SPAN class="verseno">17 </SPAN>During one of those days, this is what happened. He was teaching, Separatists and law teachers were sitting there (they had come from every village of Galilee and Judea, and from Jerusalem), and the Master's ability to cure was there.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 5:18"></A><SPAN class="verseno">18 </SPAN>And, look, outside some men were carrying a disabled man on a cot. They were looking for a way to carry him in and place him where Jesus could see him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 5:19"></A><SPAN class="verseno">19 </SPAN>When they couldn't find a way to carry him in because of the crowd, they climbed up on top of the house and let him down with the bedding through the clay tiles into the middle of the room in front of Jesus.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 5:20"></A><SPAN class="verseno">20 </SPAN>When He saw their trust, He said, "Sir, your sins have been forgiven."</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 5:21"></A><SPAN class="verseno">21 </SPAN>The Old Testament transcribers and Separatists began pondering this. They were saying, "Who is this? He is speaking insults <I>of God</I>. <I>It is obvious that God crippled this man for being a terrible sinner.</I> Who can forgive sins? Only God."</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 5:22"></A><SPAN class="verseno">22 </SPAN>After Jesus correctly understood their ponderings, He responded by saying to them, "What are you pondering in your hearts?</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 5:23"></A><SPAN class="verseno">23 </SPAN>Which is easier to say, 'Your sins have been forgiven,' or, 'Get up and walk around?'</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 5:24"></A><SPAN class="verseno">24 </SPAN>But so that you may realize that the Son of the Person has authority on the earth to be forgiving sins...." He said to the disabled man, "I tell you, Get up and pick up your bedding. Travel to your house."</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 5:25"></A><SPAN class="verseno">25 </SPAN>At once, he got up (they all watched him), picked up what he was lying down on, and went off to his house praising God's magnificence.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 5:26"></A><SPAN class="verseno">26 </SPAN>Absolutely everyone was astonished. They were praising God's magnificence and were filled with awe, "We saw unusual things today," they said.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 5:27"></A><SPAN class="verseno">27 </SPAN>After these things, as He left, He saw a tax collector (his name was Levi) sitting at the tax booth. "Follow Me," He told him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 5:28"></A><SPAN class="verseno">28 </SPAN>He left everything there, got up, and started following Him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 5:29"></A><SPAN class="verseno">29 </SPAN>Levi had a large reception for Jesus at his house. A big crowd of tax collectors and others were there lounging with them.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 5:30"></A><SPAN class="verseno">30 </SPAN>The Separatists and their Old Testament transcribers were whispering to His students: "Why are you eating and drinking with tax collectors and sinful people?"</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 5:31"></A><SPAN class="verseno">31 </SPAN>Jesus responded by telling them, "Healthy people don't need a doctor, but the people who have something wrong with them do.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 5:32"></A><SPAN class="verseno">32 </SPAN>I have not come to invite people who do what is right to change their ways. I have come to invite sinful people to change their ways."</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 5:33"></A><SPAN class="verseno">33 </SPAN>They said to Him, "John's students frequently abstain from eating and plead to God. Likewise, the Separatists' students also do this, but Yours eat and drink."</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 5:34"></A><SPAN class="verseno">34 </SPAN>Jesus told them, "You can't make the 'sons of the bridal room' <I>(the people negotiating with the groom for the bride and helping her with the wedding)</I> abstain from eating while the groom is with them, can you? <I>No, eating is a big part of the negotiation process and the wedding.</I>"</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 5:35"></A><SPAN class="verseno">35 </SPAN>But days will come when the groom is gone. Then they will be able to abstain from eating in those days."</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 5:36"></A><SPAN class="verseno">36 </SPAN>He also was telling them an illustration, "No one puts a patch torn from a new robe on a worn-out robe. If that were done, both robes would definitely be ruined. The new robe would be torn, and the worn-out robe would have a patch on it that doesn't match.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 5:37"></A><SPAN class="verseno">37 </SPAN>And no one puts wine that is in the early stages of fermentation into worn-out leather bags. If that were done, the wine would definitely rip the leather bags, it would spill out, and the leather bags would be ruined.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 5:38"></A><SPAN class="verseno">38 </SPAN>But wine that is in the early stages of fermentation must be put into new leather bags.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 5:39"></A><SPAN class="verseno">39 </SPAN>And no one after drinking fermented wine wants wine that is in the early stages of fermentation. You see, they will say that the fermented wine is useful."</P>
<TITLE>Luke 6</TITLE>
<P><A NAME="Luke 6:1"></A><SPAN class="verseno">1 </SPAN>He happened to be traveling through croplands on a Sabbath. His students were pulling the heads of grain <I>off the plants</I>, rubbing them in their hands <I>to remove the husks</I>, and eating the grain.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 6:2"></A><SPAN class="verseno">2 </SPAN>"Why are you all doing what is not allowed on the Sabbaths?" asked some of the Separatists.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 6:3"></A><SPAN class="verseno">3 </SPAN>When Jesus answered them, He said, "Didn't you even read this thing that David did when he and those with him were hungry?</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 6:4"></A><SPAN class="verseno">4 </SPAN><I>Didn't you read</I> how he went into God's house, took the display bread, ate it, and gave it to the people with him? No one is allowed to eat the display bread except the priests. <I>Why don't you condemn David for what he did when he was hungry?</I>"</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 6:5"></A><SPAN class="verseno">5 </SPAN>He was also telling them, "The Son of the Person is the Sabbath's Master." <I>("The Son of the Person" is a generic term Jesus used of Himself. Ezekiel and Daniel were called "son of a person." "Son of a person" is also in Psalm 80:17.)</I></P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 6:6"></A><SPAN class="verseno">6 </SPAN>On a different Sabbath, He happened to go into the synagogue and teach. A man was there whose right hand was deformed.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 6:7"></A><SPAN class="verseno">7 </SPAN>The Old Testament transcribers and Separatists were watching Him closely to see if He would heal on the Sabbath. They were looking for a way to level a complaint against Him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 6:8"></A><SPAN class="verseno">8 </SPAN>He realized their ponderings. He told the man who had the deformed hand, "Get up and stand in the middle." He got up and stood in the middle.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 6:9"></A><SPAN class="verseno">9 </SPAN>"I ask you," Jesus said to them, "when it comes to the Sabbath, which is allowed: to do good or to do bad, to rescue a soul or to ruin a soul?"</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 6:10"></A><SPAN class="verseno">10 </SPAN>After He looked around at them all, He told him, "Put out your hand." He did, and his hand was established back to normal.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 6:11"></A><SPAN class="verseno">11 </SPAN>They were filled with insanity and were speaking in detail with each other about what they should do to Jesus.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 6:12"></A><SPAN class="verseno">12 </SPAN>On one of these days, He happened to go out into the mountain to pray. He continued through the night praying to God.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 6:13"></A><SPAN class="verseno">13 </SPAN>When day came, He hollered for His students. He selected twelve of them and gave them the name, missionaries. <I>He named them this because He was going to be sending them out on errands, on missions.</I></P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 6:14"></A><SPAN class="verseno">14 </SPAN>They were Simon (that He also named Peter), Andrew (his brother), James, John, Philip, Bartholomew,</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 6:15"></A><SPAN class="verseno">15 </SPAN>Matthew, Thomas, James (Alphaeus' son), Simon (the one called Zealot),</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 6:16"></A><SPAN class="verseno">16 </SPAN>Judas (James's brother), and Judas from Kerioth (who became a traitor).</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 6:17"></A><SPAN class="verseno">17 </SPAN>He walked down the mountain with them and stopped on a level area. A big crowd of His students and a very large number of the ethnic group were there from all of Judea, Jerusalem, and the sea coast of Tyre and Sidon. They came to listen to Him and to be cured of their illnesses.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 6:18"></A><SPAN class="verseno">18 </SPAN>He was healing people bothered by spirits that are not clean.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 6:19"></A><SPAN class="verseno">19 </SPAN>The entire crowd were looking for a way to touch Him because <I>the</I> ability <I>to heal</I> was coming out directly from Him and curing everyone.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 6:20"></A><SPAN class="verseno">20 </SPAN>He looked up at His students and said, "You who are poor have a blessing because God's monarchy is yours.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 6:21"></A><SPAN class="verseno">21 </SPAN>You who are hungry now have a blessing because you will be full. You who are crying now have a blessing because you will laugh.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 6:22"></A><SPAN class="verseno">22 </SPAN>You are blessed when people hate you and when they isolate you, criticize you, and throw out your name as evil because of the Son of the Person.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 6:23"></A><SPAN class="verseno">23 </SPAN>Be happy in that day and skip <I>for joy</I>. You see, look, your pay is much in heaven. Their fathers were doing the same thing to the preachers.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 6:24"></A><SPAN class="verseno">24 </SPAN>More importantly, a tragedy to you wealthy people is that you have all of your comfort.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 6:25"></A><SPAN class="verseno">25 </SPAN>A tragedy to you who are filled up now is that you will be hungry. A tragedy to you who are laughing now is that you will grieve and cry.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 6:26"></A><SPAN class="verseno">26 </SPAN>What a tragedy it is when all the people talk nicely of you. You see, their fathers were doing the same thing to the counterfeit preachers.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 6:27"></A><SPAN class="verseno">27 </SPAN>But I tell you, you who are listening, love your enemies. Do nice things to the people who hate you.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 6:28"></A><SPAN class="verseno">28 </SPAN>Confer a blessing on the people who are hoping that something bad will happen to you. Pray for the people who are spiteful of you.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 6:29"></A><SPAN class="verseno">29 </SPAN>If someone hits you on the cheek, allow him to hit you on the other cheek too. If someone takes your robe, don't keep him from taking your long undershirt too.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 6:30"></A><SPAN class="verseno">30 </SPAN>When someone asks you for something, give it to him. When someone takes something that is yours, don't ask for it back.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 6:31"></A><SPAN class="verseno">31 </SPAN>Treat people in the same way <I>and</I> just as you also want them to treat you.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 6:32"></A><SPAN class="verseno">32 </SPAN>If you love the people who love you, what kind of generosity are you showing? You see, even sinful people love the people who love them.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 6:33"></A><SPAN class="verseno">33 </SPAN>And if you do good things for the people who do good things for you, what kind of generosity are you showing? Even sinful people do that.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 6:34"></A><SPAN class="verseno">34 </SPAN>If you give an interest loan to people you anticipate to receive from, what kind of generosity are you showing? Even sinful people give an interest loan to sinful people so that they will receive the things that are equal <I>to the full amount plus interest</I>.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 6:35"></A><SPAN class="verseno">35 </SPAN>More importantly, love your enemies, do good, and give an interest loan anticipating nothing back. Then your pay will be much, and you will be sons of the Highest because He is kind to the ungenerous and evil people.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 6:36"></A><SPAN class="verseno">36 </SPAN>Become compassionate just as your Father also is compassionate.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 6:37"></A><SPAN class="verseno">37 </SPAN>Don't judge, and you won't in any way be judged. Don't find people guilty, and you won't in any way be found guilty. Dismiss <I>people from what they should have done</I>, and you will be dismissed <I>from what you should have done</I>.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 6:38"></A><SPAN class="verseno">38 </SPAN>Give, and it will be given to you. They will give a nice amount that has been packed down and shaken together with even more spilling out over into your lap. You see, the amount that you measure out will be the amount measured back to you."</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 6:39"></A><SPAN class="verseno">39 </SPAN>He also told them this illustration: "A blind person can't guide a blind person, can he? Won't both fall into a hole?</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 6:40"></A><SPAN class="verseno">40 </SPAN>A student isn't above his teacher, but everyone fully developed by a teacher will be like his teacher.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 6:41"></A><SPAN class="verseno">41 </SPAN>Why do you see the wood chip in your brother's eye <I>(his tiny fault)</I>, but don't take a close look at the log in your own eye <I>(your huge fault)?</I></P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 6:42"></A><SPAN class="verseno">42 </SPAN>How can you say to your brother, 'Brother, allow me to take out the wood chip in your eye,' when you yourself don't see the log in your eye? Faker, first take the log out of your eye, and then you'll see clearly to take out the wood chip in your brother's eye.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 6:43"></A><SPAN class="verseno">43 </SPAN>You see, a nice tree doesn't produce defective fruit, and a defective tree doesn't produce nice fruit.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 6:44"></A><SPAN class="verseno">44 </SPAN>Each tree is known by the fruit that it produces. <I>Figs and grapes are fruits.</I> People don't gather figs from thorn bushes. <I>Figs are on trees that don't have thorns.</I> They don't pick a cluster of grapes from a bush either. <I>Grapes are on vines.</I></P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 6:45"></A><SPAN class="verseno">45 </SPAN>A good person brings out good things from his stockpile of good, and an evil person brings out evil things from his stockpile of evil. You see, his mouth speaks from the excess in his heart.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 6:46"></A><SPAN class="verseno">46 </SPAN>Why do you call Me, Master, Master, and don't do what I say?</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 6:47"></A><SPAN class="verseno">47 </SPAN>Everyone who comes to Me, who listens to My messages, and who does them, I will put in front of your face who he is like.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 6:48"></A><SPAN class="verseno">48 </SPAN>He is like a person building a house, who excavated, went deep, and set a foundation on the bedrock. When a torrential rain came, the river crashed against that house and couldn't disturb it because it was nicely built.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 6:49"></A><SPAN class="verseno">49 </SPAN>But the person who listens and does not do, is like a person who built a house on the soil without a foundation. When the river crashed against it, right away it collapsed. The crash of that house became great.</P>
<TITLE>Luke 7</TITLE>
<P><A NAME="Luke 7:1"></A><SPAN class="verseno">1 </SPAN>Since He, for sure, filled up what the group heard with all His statements, He went into Capernaum.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 7:2"></A><SPAN class="verseno">2 </SPAN>A certain lieutenant's slave had something wrong with him and was going to pass away. The slave was important to him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 7:3"></A><SPAN class="verseno">3 </SPAN>When the lieutenant heard about Jesus, he sent the Jewish people's older men out to Him asking Him to come and completely restore his slave.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 7:4"></A><SPAN class="verseno">4 </SPAN>When the <I>older men</I> showed up to <I>where</I> Jesus <I>was</I>, they were aggressively encouraging Him to go, saying that he deserves it.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 7:5"></A><SPAN class="verseno">5 </SPAN>"You see, he loves our nation," they told Him, "and he built the synagogue for us."</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 7:6"></A><SPAN class="verseno">6 </SPAN>Jesus traveled to his house with them. As He already was not far away from the house, the lieutenant sent friends telling Him, "Master, don't be irritated. You see, I am unfit for you to come in under the roof of my house.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 7:7"></A><SPAN class="verseno">7 </SPAN>For this reason, I also didn't think that I deserved to come to You. But say the word, and my servant boy will have to be cured.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 7:8"></A><SPAN class="verseno">8 </SPAN>You see, even though I am a person arranged under the authority <I>of the Roman Emperor</I>, I have soldiers under me. I say, 'Travel,' to this one, and he travels. I say, 'Go,' to another, and he goes. <P><A NAME="Luke 9:29"></A><SPAN class="verseno">29 </SPAN>While He was praying, His face became visually different, and His clothes turned sparkling white.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 9:30"></A><SPAN class="verseno">30 </SPAN>And, look, two men were speaking together with Him: Moses and Elijah.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 9:31"></A><SPAN class="verseno">31 </SPAN>There was a glow of magnificence in the way they looked. They were talking about His exit that was going to be accomplished in Jerusalem.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 9:32"></A><SPAN class="verseno">32 </SPAN>Peter and the two with him had been weighted down with sleep. When they completely woke up, they saw His magnificence and the two men that had been standing together with Him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 9:33"></A><SPAN class="verseno">33 </SPAN>During the <I>time</I> that the <I>two</I> happened to be completely separated away from <I>Jesus</I>, Peter told Him, "Boss, it is nice for us to be here. Let's make three tents, one for You, one for Moses, and one for Elijah." He didn't realize what he was saying.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 9:34"></A><SPAN class="verseno">34 </SPAN>As he said this, a cloud formed and shined over them. They were afraid as they entered the cloud.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 9:35"></A><SPAN class="verseno">35 </SPAN>A voice came from the cloud, saying, "This is My Son. I have selected Him. Listen to Him."</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 9:36"></A><SPAN class="verseno">36 </SPAN>After the voice, Jesus was found to be alone. The three students kept quiet and didn't report anything to anyone in those days about what they had seen.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 9:37"></A><SPAN class="verseno">37 </SPAN>On the next day, after they came down from the mountain, a big crowd happened to meet together with Him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 9:38"></A><SPAN class="verseno">38 </SPAN>And, look, a man from the crowd shouted, "Teacher, I am pleading with You, take a look at my son because he is my only biological son.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 9:39"></A><SPAN class="verseno">39 </SPAN>Look, a spirit takes him, he unexpectedly yells, it sends him into convulsions, foam comes out of his mouth, he expends a lot of effort, and he is crushed by the time it distances itself away from him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 9:40"></A><SPAN class="verseno">40 </SPAN>I pleaded with Your students to throw it out, but they weren't able to."</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 9:41"></A><SPAN class="verseno">41 </SPAN>When Jesus answered, He said, "O, untrusting and twisted generation, how long must I be near you and tolerate you? Bring your son here to Me."</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 9:42"></A><SPAN class="verseno">42 </SPAN>As he was still coming, the lesser deity ripped him and sent him into violent convulsions. Jesus stopped the spirit that was not clean, cured the boy, and gave him back to his father.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 9:43"></A><SPAN class="verseno">43 </SPAN>Everyone was impressed with the greatness of God. Since everyone was amazed by all the things that He was doing, He told His students,</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 9:44"></A><SPAN class="verseno">44 </SPAN>"You must put these words in your ears. You see, people are going to take the Son of the Person into custody."</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 9:45"></A><SPAN class="verseno">45 </SPAN>The students were unaware of what this statement meant. It had been concealed from them so that they wouldn't comprehend it, and they were afraid to ask Him about it.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 9:46"></A><SPAN class="verseno">46 </SPAN>There was a pondering that came in among them: which of them would be the greatest.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 9:47"></A><SPAN class="verseno">47 </SPAN>When Jesus realized what they were pondering in their heart, He latched on to a young child and stood him beside Him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 9:48"></A><SPAN class="verseno">48 </SPAN>"Whoever accepts this young child based on My name accepts Me," He told them, "and whoever accepts Me accepts the One who sent Me out. You see, the person who is littler among you all, this person is great."</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 9:49"></A><SPAN class="verseno">49 </SPAN>"Boss," responded John, "we saw someone throwing out lesser deities in Your name, and we were keeping him from doing it because he isn't following with us."</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 9:50"></A><SPAN class="verseno">50 </SPAN>"Don't keep him from doing it," Jesus told him. "You see, someone who is not against you is over with you."</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 9:51"></A><SPAN class="verseno">51 </SPAN>In observance of the days of His being taken up <I>to heaven</I>, it happened that He also was determined to travel directly to Jerusalem.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 9:52"></A><SPAN class="verseno">52 </SPAN>He sent messengers out ahead of Him. The messengers traveled into a village of Samaritans to get things ready for Him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 9:53"></A><SPAN class="verseno">53 </SPAN>They didn't accepted Him <I>or His request to spend the night there</I> because He appeared to be traveling into Jerusalem. <I>(This could have been due to their rivalry with Jerusalem or because they wanted Jesus to spend several days with them, not just one night.)</I></P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 9:54"></A><SPAN class="verseno">54 </SPAN>When His students, James and John, saw it, they said, "Master, do you want us to tell fire to step down out of the sky and consume them?"</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 9:55"></A><SPAN class="verseno">55 </SPAN>He turned around and shushed them.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 9:56"></A><SPAN class="verseno">56 </SPAN>They traveled to a different village.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 9:57"></A><SPAN class="verseno">57 </SPAN>As they traveled on the road, someone told Him, "I will follow You wherever You go off to."</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 9:58"></A><SPAN class="verseno">58 </SPAN>"Foxes have burrows," Jesus told him, "and the birds of the sky have nests, but the Son of the Person doesn't even have a place to rest His head."</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 9:59"></A><SPAN class="verseno">59 </SPAN>He told a different person, "Follow Me." But that person said, "Master, give me permission to first go off and bury my father <I>after he dies</I>."</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 9:60"></A><SPAN class="verseno">60 </SPAN>"Leave the dead to bury their own dead," Jesus told him. "You must go and announce God's monarchy everywhere."</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 9:61"></A><SPAN class="verseno">61 </SPAN>A different person also said, "I will follow you, Master, but first give me permission to go back home and spend a few days telling everyone good-bye."</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 9:62"></A><SPAN class="verseno">62 </SPAN>But Jesus told him, "No one who is guiding a plow with his hands and looking back at where he left his stuff is suitable for God's monarchy."</P>
<TITLE>Luke 10</TITLE>
<P><A NAME="Luke 10:1"></A><SPAN class="verseno">1 </SPAN>After this, the Master showed everyone seventy different ones. He sent them out by twos on a mission to go ahead of Him into every city and every place where He was going to be going.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 10:2"></A><SPAN class="verseno">2 </SPAN>He was telling them, "There certainly is a big harvest, but there are <I>only</I> a few workers. So plead with the master of the harvest so that he might put workers out into his harvest.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 10:3"></A><SPAN class="verseno">3 </SPAN>Make your way out. Look, I am sending you out as lambs in the middle of wolves <I>(the vulnerable among the dangerous)</I>.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 10:4"></A><SPAN class="verseno">4 </SPAN>Don't haul a money bag, tote bag, or sandals around. Don't greet anyone along the way.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 10:5"></A><SPAN class="verseno">5 </SPAN>Whenever you go into a house, first say, "Peace to this house."</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 10:6"></A><SPAN class="verseno">6 </SPAN>And if a son of peace is there, your peace will relax on it. But if <I>a son of peace is</I> definitely not there <I>(if they want to argue, fight, or get upset), your peace</I> will double back on to you <I>(or in other words, quietly leave--leave in peace, just as you came)</I>.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 10:7"></A><SPAN class="verseno">7 </SPAN>Stay in the same house eating and drinking what they provide. You see, the worker deserves his pay. Do not go from house to house.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 10:8"></A><SPAN class="verseno">8 </SPAN>In whatever city you go to and they accept you, eat what they place in front of you,</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 10:9"></A><SPAN class="verseno">9 </SPAN>heal the frail people in it, and tell them, "God's monarchy has come near over you."</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 10:10"></A><SPAN class="verseno">10 </SPAN>But in whatever city you go to and they don't accept you, go out into its plaza and say,</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 10:11"></A><SPAN class="verseno">11 </SPAN>'Even your city's dust that is stuck to our feet, we are wiping off against you. But the more important thing you should know is that God's monarchy has come near over you.'</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 10:12"></A><SPAN class="verseno">12 </SPAN>I tell you that it will be more tolerable for Sodom in that day than it will be for that city.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 10:13"></A><SPAN class="verseno">13 </SPAN>What a tragedy it is to you, Chorazin! What a tragedy it is to you, Bethsaida! because if the abilities that happened among you happened in Tyre and Sidon, they would have changed their ways a long time ago wearing sackcloth <I>(the cloth that grieving people wear)</I> and sitting in ashes <I>to express their grief</I>.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 10:14"></A><SPAN class="verseno">14 </SPAN>More importantly, it will be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon in the sentencing than for you.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 10:15"></A><SPAN class="verseno">15 </SPAN>And you, Capernaum, you will not be put up high, up to heaven, <I>as you think you will, just because I was often in your city</I>. You will be walked down to Hades <I>(the underworld of the dead)</I>.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 10:16"></A><SPAN class="verseno">16 </SPAN>The person who listens to you listens to Me, and the person who disregards you disregards Me. The person who disregards Me disregards the One who sent Me out on a mission to this earth."</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 10:17"></A><SPAN class="verseno">17 </SPAN>When the seventy returned, they were happy. "Master, even the lesser deities place themselves under us in Your name," they said.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 10:18"></A><SPAN class="verseno">18 </SPAN>"I was watching the Opponent fall from the sky as lightning," He told them.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 10:19"></A><SPAN class="verseno">19 </SPAN>"Look, I have given you the authority to trample up on top of snakes and scorpions and up on top of every ability of the enemy. Nothing will harm you in any way.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 10:20"></A><SPAN class="verseno">20 </SPAN>More importantly, don't be happy about this, that the spirits place themselves under you. Be happy that your names have been written in heaven."</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 10:21"></A><SPAN class="verseno">21 </SPAN>In that same hour, He was excited in the Sacred Spirit and said, "I admire the way You, Father, Master of heaven and earth, hid these things from the scholars and scientists and uncovered them to infants. Yes, Father, as You have seen, this has worked out quite well.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 10:22"></A><SPAN class="verseno">22 </SPAN>My Father turned everything over to Me. No one knows who the Son is except the Father. And no one knows who the Father is except the Son and whoever the Son intends to uncover Him to."</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 10:23"></A><SPAN class="verseno">23 </SPAN>He turned toward His students privately and said, "The eyes that see what you see are blessed.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 10:24"></A><SPAN class="verseno">24 </SPAN>You see, I tell you that many preachers and kings wanted to see what you are looking at and didn't. They wanted to hear what you hear and didn't."</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 10:25"></A><SPAN class="verseno">25 </SPAN>And look, a certain law expert stood up, intentionally harassing Him. "Teacher," he said, "what is one thing that after I do it I will inherit life that spans all time?"</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 10:26"></A><SPAN class="verseno">26 </SPAN>Jesus said to him, "What has been written in the law? How do you read it?"</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 10:27"></A><SPAN class="verseno">27 </SPAN>When the law expert answered, he said, "You will love the Master, your God, from your whole heart, in your whole soul, in your whole strength, and in your whole mind, and the person near you as yourself."</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 10:28"></A><SPAN class="verseno">28 </SPAN>"You answered correctly," He told him. "Do this and you will live."</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 10:29"></A><SPAN class="verseno">29 </SPAN>But the law expert wanted to show that he was doing the right thing <I>because the people near him were good people. They were priests and Levites and he loved them. To flaunt this</I>, he asked Jesus, "And who is near me?"</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 10:30"></A><SPAN class="verseno">30 </SPAN>When Jesus took it up, He said, "A certain person was walking down out of Jerusalem to Jericho. On his way there, bandits surrounded him, stripped him of everything, and put wounds on him, leaving him half dead.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 10:31"></A><SPAN class="verseno">31 </SPAN>By coincidence a certain priest was walking down to Jericho on that same road. When he saw him, he passed by on the other side.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 10:32"></A><SPAN class="verseno">32 </SPAN>Likewise, a Levite also happened to come to that place. After he went over and looked at him, he passed by on the other side.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 10:33"></A><SPAN class="verseno">33 </SPAN>But as a certain Samaritan was on a trip, when he went by him and saw him, he had sympathy for him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 10:34"></A><SPAN class="verseno">34 </SPAN>He went over to him, poured olive oil and wine on his wounds, and bandaged them up. Then he loaded him onto his own animal, took him into an inn, and took care of him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 10:35"></A><SPAN class="verseno">35 </SPAN>On the next day, he took out two denarii <I>(coins equal to one day's wage apiece)</I>, and gave them to the innkeeper. 'Take care of him,' he told him, 'and if you spend more than that on him, when I come back by here, I will pay you back.'</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 10:36"></A><SPAN class="verseno">36 </SPAN>Which of these three do you think became near to the man who fell into the bandits?"</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 10:37"></A><SPAN class="verseno">37 </SPAN>"The one who showed him forgiving kindness," he said. "Travel, and do the same thing," Jesus told him. <I>(The real question is not, 'Who is near me?' but, 'Will I become near to the people near me?')</I></P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 10:38"></A><SPAN class="verseno">38 </SPAN>During the time that they were traveling, He went into a certain village. A certain woman was there named Martha. She invited Him to stay in her house.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 10:39"></A><SPAN class="verseno">39 </SPAN><I>Martha</I> had a sister named Mary. Mary was seated beside the Master at His feet listening to His message.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 10:40"></A><SPAN class="verseno">40 </SPAN>Martha was being pulled <I>all</I> around with much serving. She stood over <I>Him</I> and said, "Master, aren't you concerned that my sister has left me back here to serve alone? So, talk to her so that she will get together with me and assist me."</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 10:41"></A><SPAN class="verseno">41 </SPAN>"Martha, Martha," the Master answered, "you are worried and flustered about many things,</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 10:42"></A><SPAN class="verseno">42 </SPAN>but there is one thing that's needed. You see, Mary selected the good part, something that won't be taken away from her."</P>
<TITLE>Luke 11</TITLE>
<P><A NAME="Luke 11:1"></A><SPAN class="verseno">1 </SPAN>During the time that He happened to be in a certain place praying, when He stopped, one of His students said to Him, "Master, teach us how to pray, just as John also taught his students."</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 11:2"></A><SPAN class="verseno">2 </SPAN>"When you pray," He told them, "say, Father, Your name <I>and who You are</I> must be made sacred. Your monarchy must come.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 11:3"></A><SPAN class="verseno">3 </SPAN>You must give us the daily thing, our next day's bread.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 11:4"></A><SPAN class="verseno">4 </SPAN>And You must forgive us of our sins. You see, we ourselves also forgive everyone who owes us. And You won't carry us into trouble."</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 11:5"></A><SPAN class="verseno">5 </SPAN>He also told them, "What if someone from among you will have a friend and he will travel to him in the middle of the night? He might tell him, 'Friend, loan me three loaves of bread</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 11:6"></A><SPAN class="verseno">6 </SPAN>since, for sure, a friend of mine showed up at my house in the middle of his trip and I don't have any food to place in front of him.'</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 11:7"></A><SPAN class="verseno">7 </SPAN>When that friend answers from inside, he could say, 'Don't bother me. I've already locked the door and my young children are with me in bed <I>asleep in my arms</I>. I can't get up and give you <I>some bread</I>.'</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 11:8"></A><SPAN class="verseno">8 </SPAN>I tell you, even if the fact that he is his friend won't cause him to get up and give him some bread, the fact that he had the nerve to knock on his door in the middle of the night definitely will. He will give him as much as he needs.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 11:9"></A><SPAN class="verseno">9 </SPAN>I tell you, ask, and it will be given to you. Look, and you will find. Knock, and <I>a door</I> will be opened for you.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 11:10"></A><SPAN class="verseno">10 </SPAN>You see, everyone asking receives. The person looking finds. And <I>a door</I> will open to the person knocking.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 11:11"></A><SPAN class="verseno">11 </SPAN>Any father from among you, if your son asks for a fish, will you give him a snake instead?</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 11:12"></A><SPAN class="verseno">12 </SPAN>Or if he asks for an egg, will you give him a scorpion?</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 11:13"></A><SPAN class="verseno">13 </SPAN>So if you all who are evil know that you should be giving good presents to your children, how much more will the Father from heaven give the Sacred Spirit to the people who ask Him" <I>(the Sacred Spirit that also provides good presents)</I>?</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 11:14"></A><SPAN class="verseno">14 </SPAN>He was throwing out a lesser deity from a man who couldn't speak. It happened that when the lesser deity came out, the speech-impaired man spoke. The crowds were amazed.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 11:15"></A><SPAN class="verseno">15 </SPAN>Some in the crowd said, "He throws the lesser deities out with the help of Beelzebub, the head of the lesser deities."</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 11:16"></A><SPAN class="verseno">16 </SPAN>Different ones were harassing Him looking for a proof <I>to come</I> out of the sky directly from Him.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 11:17"></A><SPAN class="verseno">17 </SPAN>He, realizing their thoughts, told them, "Every monarchy that is divided up and disagrees with itself becomes uninhabited, and a house disagreeing with a house, falls.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 11:18"></A><SPAN class="verseno">18 </SPAN>If the Opponent also has been divided up and disagrees with itself, how will his monarchy be established? <I>I am making this point</I> because you say that I am throwing the lesser deities out with the help of Beelzebub. <I>Look at what I am doing. Look at what I am teaching. It disagrees with Beelzebub.</I></P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 11:19"></A><SPAN class="verseno">19 </SPAN>If I throw the lesser deities out with the help of Beelzebub, what about your sons? With whom do they throw them out? <I>Ask them. Their answers</I> will stand as judges of you.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 11:20"></A><SPAN class="verseno">20 </SPAN>But if I throw the lesser deities out with God's finger, clearly God's monarchy has already come to you.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 11:21"></A><SPAN class="verseno">21 </SPAN>When a fully armored strong person guards his courtyard, his things are safe.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 11:22"></A><SPAN class="verseno">22 </SPAN>But whenever someone stronger than the strong person comes up against him, he conquers him, takes his full body armor that gave him confidence, and passes out his spoils. <I>I am able to throw out lesser deities because I am using God's finger and it is stronger than the Opponent.</I></P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 11:23"></A><SPAN class="verseno">23 </SPAN>The person who is not with Me is against Me, and the person who does not gather with Me scatters My things.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 11:24"></A><SPAN class="verseno">24 </SPAN>When a spirit that is not clean leaves a person, it passes through places that don't have water looking for relief. And not finding it, it says, 'I will return back into my house that I left.'</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 11:25"></A><SPAN class="verseno">25 </SPAN>When it arrives, it finds that the house has been swept and decorated.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 11:26"></A><SPAN class="verseno">26 </SPAN>Then it travels, finds seven different spirits more evil than itself, and brings them along. When they go in, they live there, and it becomes <I>such that</I> the last <I>circumstances</I> of that person are worse than the first."</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 11:27"></A><SPAN class="verseno">27 </SPAN>During the time that He was saying these things, it happened that a certain woman from the crowd raised her voice and said, "The belly that hauled You around and the breasts that nursed You are blessed."</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 11:28"></A><SPAN class="verseno">28 </SPAN>He said, "So, of course, the people hearing and observing God's message are blessed."</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 11:29"></A><SPAN class="verseno">29 </SPAN>As the crowds gathered more <I>people</I>, He began to be saying, "This generation is an evil generation. It is searching for proof <I>that God sent Me</I>. No proof will be given to it except the proof of Jonah.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 11:30"></A><SPAN class="verseno">30 </SPAN>You see, just as Jonah became proof to the Ninevites, so the Son of the Person will also be proof to this generation.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 11:31"></A><SPAN class="verseno">31 </SPAN>In the sentencing with the men of this generation, a queen from the south will get up and find them guilty because she came from the ends of the earth to hear Solomon's insight and, look, a greater thing than Solomon is here.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 11:32"></A><SPAN class="verseno">32 </SPAN>In the sentencing with this generation, Ninevite men will stand up and find it guilty because they changed their ways and did what Jonah yelled on their streets and, look, a greater thing than Jonah is here.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 11:33"></A><SPAN class="verseno">33 </SPAN>No one lights a lamp and puts it in a hidden place or under the two gallon measuring basket. No, it is put up high on a stand so that the people traveling into the room may see the light.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 11:34"></A><SPAN class="verseno">34 </SPAN>Light enters the body through the eye. Your eye is the body's lamp. When your eye is dedicated <I>to its job of seeing</I>, your whole body is lit up. But whenever it is evil <I>and refuses to do its job correctly</I>, your body is dark.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 11:35"></A><SPAN class="verseno">35 </SPAN>So look out for this: that the light in you is not darkness.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 11:36"></A><SPAN class="verseno">36 </SPAN>If your whole body is lit up, not having any dark spots, it will be lit up as when a lamp as bright as lightning lights things up for you."</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 11:37"></A><SPAN class="verseno">37 </SPAN>During the time that He was speaking, a Separatist asked Him to have lunch at his house. When He went in, He settled down on one of the sofas.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 11:38"></A><SPAN class="verseno">38 </SPAN>When the Separatist saw this, he was amazed that He had not first submerged Himself in water before lunch. <I>Jews submerge themselves in water to make themselves ritually clean.</I></P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 11:39"></A><SPAN class="verseno">39 </SPAN>The Master said to him, "Now you Separatists clean the outside of the cup and the plate, but your inside is still packed full of looting and evilness.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 11:40"></A><SPAN class="verseno">40 </SPAN>Aren't you distracted? When God made the outside of you, didn't He also make the inside? <I>Why aren't you concerned about your inside?</I></P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 11:41"></A><SPAN class="verseno">41 </SPAN>A more important thing is to give the things inside of you as a charitable donation. <I>Let go of them.</I> Then, look, everything will be clean for you.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 11:42"></A><SPAN class="verseno">42 </SPAN>But what a tragedy it is to you, Separatists, because you make sure to give a ten-percent offering from the <I>lesser plants in your garden</I> (sweet smelling mint, rue leaves, and every vegetable) and pass by the heavier things: justice and the love of God. You must do these heavier things and not neglect those lesser ones.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 11:43"></A><SPAN class="verseno">43 </SPAN>What a tragedy it is to you, Separatists, because you love the front bench in the synagogue and people greeting you in the marketplace.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 11:44"></A><SPAN class="verseno">44 </SPAN>What a tragedy it is to you because you are like obscure burial vaults. The people walking around up on top of you do not realize that they are walking over a place of death."</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 11:45"></A><SPAN class="verseno">45 </SPAN>One of the law experts responded by telling Him, "Teacher, what you are saying also injures us."</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 11:46"></A><SPAN class="verseno">46 </SPAN>"And to you, the law experts," said Jesus, "what a tragedy it is because you load people down with heavy hard-to-haul loads and you yourselves don't even lightly touch those heavy loads with one of your fingers.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 11:47"></A><SPAN class="verseno">47 </SPAN>What a tragedy it is to you because you build the preachers' burial vaults, but your fathers killed them.</P>
<P><A NAME="Luke 11:48"></A><SPAN class="verseno">48 </SPAN>Clearly you are witnesses and agree that you think your fathers' actions were good because not only did your fathers kill them, but now you are building their burial vaults.</P>

<P><A NAME="Luke 11:52"></A><SPAN class="verseno">52 </SPAN>What a tragedy it is to you, the law experts, because you yourselves take away the key to the information. You didn't go in, and you keep the people from going in."</P>
